title.zh: 卷一百四十七 列傳第三十四: 張柔 史天倪 史天祥
title.en: Volume 147 Biographies 34: Zhang Rou, Shi Tianni, Shi Tianxiang
title.raw: 卷一百四十七 列傳第三十四: 張柔 史天倪 史天祥 Volume 147 Biographies 34: Zhang Rou, Shi Tianni, Shi Tianxiang

sentences.zh: 張柔，字德剛，易州定興人，世力農。

translations.literal: Zhang Rou, style name Degang, was a native of Dingxing in Yizhou; his family for generations labored as farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rou, styled Degang, came from Dingxing in Yizhou. His family had farmed the land for generations.

sentences.zh: 柔少慷慨，尚氣節，善騎射，以豪俠稱。

translations.literal: In his youth Rou was magnanimous, esteemed integrity and honor, excelled at mounted archery, and was known as a bold hero.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Rou was open-handed and chivalrous, prized loyalty and courage, skilled in horsemanship and archery, and famed as a gallant free spirit.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐間，河北盜起，柔聚族黨保西山東流寨，選壯士，結隊伍以自衛，盜不敢犯。

translations.literal: During the Jinyou era of Jin, bandits rose in Hebei. Rou gathered his clan to hold Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, selected strong men, formed companies for self-defense, and bandits did not dare molest them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinyou reign of the Jin, brigands spread across Hebei. Rou rallied his kinsmen to defend Dongliu Stockade in the Western Hills, picked stalwart fighters, and organized armed bands for protection so that raiders dared not trouble them.

sentences.zh: 郡人張信假柔聲勢，納流人女為妻，柔鞭信百而還其女。

translations.literal: A townsman Zhang Xin borrowed Rou's prestige, took a refugee woman as wife; Rou flogged Xin a hundred strokes and returned the woman.
translations.idiomatic: A local man named Zhang Xin traded on Rou's reputation to seize a refugee woman as his wife. Rou had Xin whipped a hundred times and sent the woman back.

sentences.zh: 信憾之，謀結黨害柔。

translations.literal: Xin bore resentment and plotted with a faction to harm Rou.
translations.idiomatic: Xin nursed a grudge and schemed with allies to destroy Rou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，信有罪當誅，柔救之得免，於是驍勇之士，多慕義從之。

translations.literal: Before long Xin committed a crime warranting execution; Rou saved him and he was spared, whereupon many fierce warriors admired his righteousness and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Xin was condemned to death for a crime, but Rou intervened and he was pardoned. From then on many bold fighters were drawn to his sense of justice and joined his cause.

sentences.zh: 中都經略使苗道潤承製授柔定興令，累遷清州防禦使。

translations.literal: The Central Capital military commissioner Miao Daorun by imperial commission appointed Rou magistrate of Dingxing; he was promoted repeatedly to Defender of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Daorun, military commissioner of the Central Capital, appointed Rou magistrate of Dingxing by imperial order, and Rou rose through successive posts to Defender of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 道潤表其才，加昭毅大將軍，遙領永定軍節度使，兼雄州管內觀察使，權元帥左都監，行元帥府事。

translations.literal: Daorun memorialized his talent; he was made Grand General of Manifest Valor, remotely bore Military Commissioner of Yongding Army, concurrently Commissioner of Observation within Xiongzhou, Acting Left Overseer of the Marshalate, and administered the Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Daorun recommended his abilities to the throne. Rou was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor, given the nominal post of Military Commissioner of the Yongding Army, made concurrent Commissioner of Observation for Xiongzhou, named acting Left Overseer of the Marshalate, and entrusted with the affairs of the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 繼而道潤為其副賈瑀所殺，瑀遣使以好辭來告曰：「吾得除道潤者，以君不助兵故也。」

translations.literal: Thereafter Daorun was killed by his deputy Jia Yu; Yu sent an envoy with conciliatory words saying: "I was able to remove Daorun because you did not aid his troops."
translations.idiomatic: Daorun was soon killed by his deputy Jia Yu, who sent an envoy with soothing words: "I was able to eliminate Daorun because you did not send troops to help him."

sentences.zh: 柔怒叱使者曰：「瑀殺吾所事，吾食瑀肉且未足快意，反以此言相戲耶！」

translations.literal: Rou angrily rebuked the envoy: "Yu killed the man I served; I would not yet be satisfied even if I ate Yu's flesh, and yet you jest with such words!"
translations.idiomatic: Rou thundered at the envoy: "Yu murdered the lord I served. I would not be satisfied even if I devoured his flesh—and you dare mock me with words like these!"

sentences.zh: 遂移檄道潤部曲，會易州軍市川，誓眾為之復仇，眾皆感泣。

translations.literal: He then issued a proclamation to Daorun's troops, assembled them at Junshichuan in Yizhou, and swore the host to avenge him; all were moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a call to arms to Daorun's troops, mustered them at Junshichuan in Yizhou, and led the host in swearing vengeance. The men wept as one.

sentences.zh: 適道潤麾下何伯祥得道潤所佩金虎符以獻，因推柔行經略使事。

translations.literal: Just then He Boxiang of Daorun's command obtained and presented the golden tiger tally Daorun had worn, and on that basis they urged Rou to act as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At that moment He Boxiang, a commander under Daorun, presented the golden tiger tally that Daorun had carried, and the troops pressed Rou to assume the duties of military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 事聞，加驃騎將軍、中都留守，兼大興府尹、本路經略使，行元帥事。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was made General of Agile Cavalry, Garrison Commander of the Central Capital, concurrently Prefect of Daxing and military commissioner of the circuit, and acted as marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry, made Garrison Commander of the Central Capital and concurrently Prefect of Daxing and military commissioner of the circuit, and entrusted with marshal's authority.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，國兵出紫荊口，柔率所部逆戰於狼牙嶺，馬蹶被執，遂以眾降，太祖還其舊職，得以便宜行事。

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the state's army issued from Zijing Pass; Rou led his troops to meet them at Langya Ridge, his horse stumbled and he was captured, then he surrendered with his host; the Taizu restored his former posts and allowed him discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day the Mongol army came through Zijing Pass. Rou met them at Langya Ridge with his forces, but his horse fell and he was taken prisoner. He then surrendered with his troops. Taizu restored his former offices and granted him broad discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 柔招集部曲，下雄、易、安、保諸州，攻破賈瑀於孔山，誅瑀，剖其心祭道潤。

translations.literal: Rou gathered his troops, descended on the prefectures of Xiong, Yi, An, and Bao, defeated Jia Yu at Kongshan, executed Yu, and cut out his heart as an offering to Daorun.
translations.idiomatic: Rou rallied his forces, swept through the prefectures of Xiong, Yi, An, and Bao, crushed Jia Yu at Kongshan, put him to death, and cut out his heart as a sacrifice to Daorun's spirit.

sentences.zh: 瑀黨郭收亦降，盡有其眾，徙治滿城。

translations.literal: Yu's partisan Guo Shou also surrendered; Rou took over all their forces and moved his seat of government to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's follower Guo Shou submitted as well. Rou absorbed their entire force and relocated his headquarters to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 金真定帥武仙會兵數万來攻，柔以兵數百出奇迎戰，大破之。

translations.literal: The Jin commander of Zhending, Wu Xian, mustered tens of thousands to attack; Rou with several hundred men struck by surprise and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian, the Jin commander at Zhending, gathered tens of thousands of troops for an assault. Rou met him with only a few hundred men in a surprise attack and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 乘勝攻完州，下之，獲州佐甄全。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory he attacked Wanzhou, took it, and captured the prefectural aide Zhen Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Following up his victory he attacked Wanzhou, captured it, and seized the prefectural aide Zhen Quan.

sentences.zh: 全慷慨就戮，柔義而釋之，且升為守，使將部曲以從。

translations.literal: Quan went to execution with noble composure; Rou in righteousness released him, moreover promoted him to defender and had him lead troops in his train.
translations.idiomatic: Quan faced execution with calm dignity. Moved by his conduct, Rou spared him, appointed him defender of the prefecture, and had him lead his own troops in Rou's service.

sentences.zh: 己卯，仙復來攻，敗走之，進拔郎山、祁州、曲陽，諸城寨聞之，皆降。

translations.literal: On the day jimao, Xian attacked again; Rou defeated and drove him off, advanced to seize Langshan, Qizhou, and Quyang, and at the news all fortresses and stockades submitted.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day Wu Xian attacked again. Rou routed him and drove him back, then advanced to take Langshan, Qizhou, and Quyang. At the news, fortresses and stockades throughout the region surrendered.

sentences.zh: 既而中山叛，柔引兵圍之，與仙將葛鐵倉戰於新樂。

translations.literal: Thereafter Zhongshan rebelled; Rou led troops to besiege it and fought Wu Xian's general Ge Tiecan at Xinle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan then rose in revolt. Rou laid siege with his army and fought Wu Xian's general Ge Tiecan at Xinle.

sentences.zh: 流矢中柔頷，折其二齒，拔矢以戰，斬首數千級，擒藁城令劉成，遂拔中山。

translations.literal: A stray arrow struck Rou's jaw and broke two teeth; he pulled out the arrow and fought on, beheading several thousand, captured Gaocheng magistrate Liu Cheng, and took Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow struck his jaw and broke two teeth. He pulled out the shaft and kept fighting, slew several thousand of the enemy, captured Liu Cheng, magistrate of Gaocheng, and finally took Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 仙復會兵攻滿城，柔登城拒戰，復為流矢所中。

translations.literal: Xian again gathered troops to attack Mancheng; Rou mounted the walls to resist and was struck once more by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian rallied his forces again to assault Mancheng. Rou defended from the walls and was hit by another stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 仙兵大呼曰：「中張柔矣！」

translations.literal: Xian's troops shouted loudly: "We have hit Zhang Rou!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian's soldiers shouted: "We have hit Zhang Rou!"

sentences.zh: 柔不為動，開門突戰，皆敗走。

translations.literal: Rou was unmoved, opened the gates for a sally, and all the enemy fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Rou did not flinch. He opened the gates and charged out; the enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 略地至鼓城，單騎入城，喻以禍福，城遂降。

translations.literal: Extending his territory to Gucheng, he entered the city alone on horseback, explained fortune and ruin, and the city thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He extended his conquests to Gucheng, rode into the city alone, explained the consequences of resistance and submission, and the city surrendered.

sentences.zh: 又敗仙於祁州，進攻深澤、寧晉、安平，克之。

translations.literal: He again defeated Xian at Qizhou, advanced to attack Shenze, Ningjin, and Anping, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Wu Xian again at Qizhou, then advanced against Shenze, Ningjin, and Anping and took them all.

sentences.zh: 分遣別將攻下平棘、藁城、無極、欒城諸縣，辟地千餘里。

translations.literal: He dispatched other generals to take the counties of Pingji, Gaocheng, Wuji, and Luancheng, opening territory of more than a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: He sent subordinate commanders to seize the counties of Pingji, Gaocheng, Wuji, and Luancheng, extending his domain by more than a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 由是深、冀以北，真定以東三十餘城，緣山反側鹿兒、野狸等寨，相繼降附。

translations.literal: Thus north of Shen and Ji, more than thirty cities east of Zhending, and mountain stockades such as Fanside, Lu'er, and Yeli, submitted one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter more than thirty cities north of Shen and Ji and east of Zhending, along with mountain strongholds such as Fanside, Lu'er, and Yeli, submitted in succession.

sentences.zh: 一月之間，與仙遇者凡十有七，每戰輒勝。

translations.literal: Within a single month he encountered Xian seventeen times in all, and in every battle prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a single month he clashed with Wu Xian seventeen times and won every encounter.

sentences.zh: 方獻捷於行在所，行次宣德，而易州軍叛，逐其守盧應妻子，據西山馬頭寨。

translations.literal: Just as he was presenting victory reports at the mobile court, halting at Xuande, the Yizhou army rebelled, drove out the defender Lu Ying's wife and children, and seized Matou Stockade in the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: While he was reporting his victories at the imperial camp, which had halted at Xuande, the Yizhou garrison mutinied, expelled the wife and children of the defender Lu Ying, and seized Matou Stockade in the Western Hills.

sentences.zh: 柔聞之，即棄輜重還，出奇計破其寨，而誅叛者，歸其妻子。

translations.literal: On hearing this Rou immediately abandoned his baggage train and returned, used a stratagem to break their stockade, executed the rebels, and restored the wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the news, Rou at once abandoned his supply train and marched back. With a surprise stratagem he stormed the stockade, executed the mutineers, and restored Lu Ying's family.

sentences.zh: 加榮祿大夫、河北東西等路都元帥，號拔都魯，置官屬，將士遷授有差。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Marshal of the Eastern and Western Hebei circuits, titled Baduru, given a staff of officials, and officers and soldiers were promoted in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Marshal of the Eastern and Western Hebei circuits, given the title Baduru, provided with a full staff, and his officers and men were rewarded with graded promotions.

sentences.zh: 燕帥孱赤台數凌柔，柔不為下，乃譖柔於中都行台曰：「張柔驍勇無敵，向被執而降，今委以兵柄，戰勝攻取，威震河朔，失今不圖，後必難制。

translations.literal: The Yan commander Chanchitai repeatedly bullied Rou, who would not yield; Chanchitai then slandered Rou to the Central Capital branch secretariat: "Zhang Rou is matchlessly fierce; though once captured he surrendered, now entrusted with military power he wins battles and takes cities, his might shaking Heshuo—if we do not deal with him now, he will later be hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan commander Chanchitai repeatedly tried to dominate Rou, who refused to submit. Chanchitai then denounced him to the Central Capital branch secretariat: "Zhang Rou is a peerless warrior. Though he surrendered after capture, he has now been given command of troops, wins every battle, and his fame shakes all of Heshuo. If we do not act now, he will prove impossible to control later.

sentences.zh: 常欲殺我，我不敢南也。」

translations.literal: He always wishes to kill me; I dare not go south."
translations.idiomatic: He has long wanted to kill me. I dare not march south while he lives."

sentences.zh: 行台召柔，幽之土室，孱赤台施帳寢其上，環以甲騎，明日將殺之，孱赤台一夕暴死，柔乃得免。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat summoned Rou and confined him in an earthen cell; Chanchitai pitched his tent to sleep above him, surrounded him with armored horsemen, and planned to kill him the next day—but Chanchitai died suddenly in one night, and Rou was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat summoned Rou and locked him in an earthen cell. Chanchitai pitched his tent above the cell, ringed it with armored cavalry, and planned to execute Rou the next day. That night Chanchitai died suddenly, and Rou was released.

sentences.zh: 金經略使固安王子昌，善戰知名，與信安張進連兵，阻水為固，遠近憚之。

translations.literal: The Jin military commissioner Wang Zichang of Gu'an was famed for skill in battle; he joined forces with Zhang Jin of Xin'an, fortified themselves behind water barriers, and men near and far feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zichang of Gu'an, a Jin military commissioner famed for his fighting skill, joined forces with Zhang Jin of Xin'an. They fortified their position behind waterways, and commanders throughout the region feared them.

sentences.zh: 柔出其不意，率兵徑渡，生擒以還。

translations.literal: Rou caught them unawares, led troops straight across the water, and captured Zichang alive.
translations.idiomatic: Rou took them by surprise, led his men straight across the water, and brought Zichang back alive as a prisoner.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，真定武仙殺其帥史天倪，其弟天澤使來求援。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou, Wu Xian of Zhending killed his commander Shi Tianni; Tianni's brother Tianze sent envoys to request aid.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Wu Xian of Zhending murdered his commander Shi Tianni. Tianni's brother Tianze sent envoys to request assistance.

sentences.zh: 柔遣驍將喬惟忠等率千餘騎赴之，與仙戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Rou dispatched the fierce general Qiao Weizhong and others with more than a thousand horsemen; they fought Xian and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Rou sent his fierce commander Qiao Weizhong and others with more than a thousand horsemen. They engaged Wu Xian and routed him.

sentences.zh: 遂分遣惟忠、宋演略彰德，徇齊魯；

translations.literal: He then separately dispatched Weizhong and Song Yan to reduce Zhangde and sweep Qi and Lu;
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Weizhong and Song Yan to reduce Zhangde and campaign through Qi and Lu;

sentences.zh: 聶福堅略青、魏、山東。

translations.literal: Nie Fujian reduced Qing, Wei, and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: and Nie Fujian to subdue Qing, Wei, and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 璽書授柔行軍千戶、保州等處都元帥。

translations.literal: An imperial patent appointed Rou Military Thousand-Household and Grand Marshal of Baozhou and other places.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict appointed Rou Military Thousand-Household and Grand Marshal of Baozhou and surrounding districts.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，遣將以兵從國王孛魯，攻李全於益都，降之。

translations.literal: On the day bingxu he sent generals with troops to follow Prince Belu, attacked Li Quan at Yidu, and received his surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day he sent commanders with troops to follow Prince Belu, attacked Li Quan at Yidu, and accepted his surrender.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，移鎮保州。

translations.literal: On the day dinghai he transferred his garrison to Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day he moved his headquarters to Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 保自兵火之餘，荒廢者十五年，盜出沒其間。

translations.literal: Since the ravages of war Baozhou had lain waste for fifteen years, with bandits coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou had lain in ruins for fifteen years since the wars, and bandits roamed the district freely.

sentences.zh: 柔為之畫市井，定民居，置官廨，引泉入城，疏溝渠以瀉卑濕，通商惠工，遂致殷富。

translations.literal: Rou laid out markets and wards for it, settled the populace, established government offices, brought springs into the city, dredged canals to drain low damp ground, opened trade and benefited craftsmen, and thus brought prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Rou planned its markets and wards, resettled the people, built government offices, brought spring water into the city, dredged canals to drain the low wet ground, encouraged trade and crafts, and restored the district to prosperity.

sentences.zh: 遷廟學於城東南，增其舊制。

translations.literal: He moved the temple school to the southeast of the city and enlarged its former scale.
translations.idiomatic: He relocated the temple school to the southeast quarter of the city and expanded it beyond its former scale.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從睿宗伐金，語其眾曰：「吾用兵，殺人多矣，寧無冤者？

translations.literal: On the day renchen he followed Ruizong in the campaign against Jin and told his troops: "In my campaigns I have killed many—can there be none wrongly slain?
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day he followed Ruizong in the campaign against Jin and addressed his troops: "In all my campaigns I have killed many men. Surely some of them were innocent.

sentences.zh: 自今以往，非與敵戰，誓不殺也。」

translations.literal: From this time forward, unless fighting the enemy, I swear I will not kill."
translations.idiomatic: From this day forward I swear that except in battle with the enemy I will take no life."

sentences.zh: 圍汴京，柔軍於城西北，金兵屢出拒戰。

translations.literal: They besieged Bianjing; Rou encamped northwest of the city, and Jin troops repeatedly sallied to resist.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Bianjing. Rou camped northwest of the city while Jin forces repeatedly sallied to fight him off.

sentences.zh: 柔單騎陷陣，出​​入數四，金人莫能支。

translations.literal: Rou alone on horseback charged the lines, going in and out four or five times, and the Jin could not withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: Rou charged the enemy lines alone on horseback, breaking in and out of the formation again and again, and the Jin troops could not hold him.

sentences.zh: 金主自黃陵岡渡河，次漚麻岡，欲取衛州，柔以兵合擊，金主敗走睢陽。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler crossed the river from Huangling Ridge, halted at Ouma Ridge intending to take Weizhou; Rou joined forces to strike him, and the Jin ruler fled in defeat to Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor crossed the Yellow River from Huangling Ridge and halted at Ouma Ridge, intending to take Weizhou. Rou joined in a combined attack and drove him in defeat toward Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 其臣崔立以汴京降，柔於金帛一無所取，獨入史館，取《金實錄》並秘府圖書；

translations.literal: His minister Cui Li surrendered Bianjing; Rou took nothing of gold or silk, but alone entered the History Office and took the Veritable Records of Jin and the secretariat books;
translations.idiomatic: His minister Cui Li surrendered Bianjing. Rou took no gold or silk for himself but went alone into the History Office and removed the Veritable Records of Jin along with the imperial library collections;

sentences.zh: 訪求耆德及燕趙故族十餘家，衛送北歸。

translations.literal: sought out more than ten families of venerable elders and old clans of Yan and Zhao, and escorted them north to return.
translations.idiomatic: sought out more than ten families of venerable elders and distinguished clans of Yan and Zhao, and escorted them safely north.

sentences.zh: 遂圍睢陽，金主走汝南。

translations.literal: He then besieged Suiyang; the Jin ruler fled to Runan.
translations.idiomatic: He then besieged Suiyang while the Jin emperor fled to Runan.

sentences.zh: 汝南恃柴潭為阻，會宋孟珙以兵糧來會，珙決其南，潭水涸。

translations.literal: Runan relied on the Chaitan moat as a barrier; meanwhile Song Meng Gong came with troops and grain to join the siege; Gong breached the south and the moat waters dried.
translations.idiomatic: Runan relied on the Chaitan moat for defense. Song Meng Gong arrived with troops and supplies to join the siege, breached the southern embankment, and the moat ran dry.

sentences.zh: 金人懼，啟南門求死戰，柔以步卒二十餘突其陣，促聶福堅先登，擒二校以歸。

translations.literal: The Jin in fear opened the south gate seeking a fight to the death; Rou with twenty-odd foot soldiers burst their formation, urged Nie Fujian to mount first, and captured two officers.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin, in desperation, opened the south gate for a final battle. Rou led a little more than twenty foot soldiers in a charge through their lines, pressed Nie Fujian to scale the wall first, and brought back two captured officers.

sentences.zh: 又遣張信據其內隍，諸軍齊進，金主自殺。

translations.literal: He also sent Zhang Xin to hold the inner moat; all armies advanced together and the Jin ruler killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Zhang Xin to seize the inner moat while the combined armies pressed forward together. The Jin emperor took his own life.

sentences.zh: 汝南既破，下令屠城，一小校縛十人以待，一人貌獨異，柔問之，狀元王鶚也，解其縛，賓禮之。

translations.literal: After Runan fell, an order went out to slaughter the city; a junior officer bound ten men awaiting execution; one man's appearance was strikingly different; Rou inquired and learned it was the top degree-holder Wang E; he released his bonds and received him as an honored guest.
translations.idiomatic: After Runan fell, orders went out to slaughter the city. A junior officer had bound ten men for execution. One man's bearing was strikingly distinguished. Rou asked who he was and learned it was Wang E, holder of the highest civil degree. He cut his bonds and received him with full honors.

sentences.zh: 入朝，太宗歷數其戰功，班諸帥上，賜金虎符，升軍民萬戶。

translations.literal: On entering court Taizong recounted his battle achievements, ranked him above the other commanders, bestowed a golden tiger tally, and promoted him to Ten-Thousand-Household of Army and People.
translations.idiomatic: At court Taizong recounted his battle honors, ranked him above the other commanders, bestowed a golden tiger tally, and promoted him to Ten-Thousand-Household of Army and People.

sentences.zh: 乙未，從皇子闊出拔棗陽，繼從大帥太赤攻徐、邳。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei he followed Prince Kuochu to take Zaoyang, then followed the grand marshal Taichi in the attack on Xu and Pi.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei day he followed Prince Kuochu to capture Zaoyang, then joined Grand Marshal Taichi in the assault on Xu and Pi.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，詔屯兵曹武以逼宋。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou an edict ordered troops stationed at Caowu to press the Song.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day an edict ordered troops stationed at Caowu to pressure the Song frontier.

sentences.zh: 道出九里關，柔欲率所部徑往，或言關甚險，宋必設伏，不若與大軍俱進。

translations.literal: The route passed Jiuli Pass; Rou wished to lead his own troops straight through; some said the pass was very perilous and the Song would surely set ambushes—it would be better to advance with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: The route passed through Jiuli Pass. Rou wanted to lead his own troops straight ahead, but others warned that the pass was treacherous and the Song would surely lay ambushes—it would be safer to march with the main army.

sentences.zh: 不聽，與二十騎直前據關，方解甲而食。

translations.literal: He would not listen, took twenty horsemen straight forward to seize the pass, and had just doffed armor to eat.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to listen, rode ahead with twenty horsemen to seize the pass, and had just dismounted to eat.

sentences.zh: 宋兵出兩山間，圍數重，騎皆失色，柔單騎馳突潰圍。

translations.literal: Song troops emerged between the two mountains and surrounded them in several rings; the horsemen all turned pale; Rou alone charged and broke the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: Song troops emerged from between the mountains and surrounded them in ring after ring. His horsemen turned pale with fear. Rou charged alone and broke through the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 大軍繼至，遂達曹武，悉下緣山諸堡，攻洪山寨，破之，遂營山下。

translations.literal: The main army arrived afterward; they reached Caowu, took all the mountain-side forts, attacked Hongshan Stockade, broke it, and encamped below the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The main army arrived soon after. They reached Caowu, reduced all the mountain forts along the route, stormed Hongshan Stockade, captured it, and made camp at the foot of the mountain.

sentences.zh: 柔率眾出略地他處，宋兵乘虛來襲，柔還，與之遇，自旦至暮，凡十餘戰，大敗宋師，斬其將校十有三人。

translations.literal: Rou led his host out to raid elsewhere; Song troops seized the moment to attack; Rou returned, met them, and from dawn to dusk fought more than ten engagements, routing the Song army and beheading thirteen of their officers.
translations.idiomatic: Rou led his men out to raid elsewhere. Song forces seized the chance to strike his camp. He returned, met them in battle, and from dawn to dusk fought more than ten engagements, crushing the Song army and slaying thirteen of their officers.

sentences.zh: 遂會諸軍取光州，又進趣黃州。

translations.literal: He then joined the armies to take Guangzhou and advanced toward Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the combined armies to take Guangzhou and advanced on Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 破三山寨，至大湖中，得戰艦，沿江接戰，壁於黃州西北隅。

translations.literal: He broke Sanshan Stockade, reached the great lake, obtained war vessels, fought along the river in succession, and fortified the northwest corner of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Sanshan Stockade, reached the great lake, seized war junks, fought a running series of engagements along the river, and fortified the northwest corner of Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有乘舟出者，柔曰：「此偵伺我隙者也，夜必襲吾不備。」

translations.literal: When someone came out in a boat Rou said: "These are spying for our gaps—they will surely attack us unawares at night."
translations.idiomatic: When a boat put out from the city, Rou said, "They are scouting our weaknesses. They will attack us by night when we are unprepared."

sentences.zh: 乃分軍為三以待之。

translations.literal: He therefore divided his army in three to await them.
translations.idiomatic: He divided his force into three detachments to await them.

sentences.zh: 二鼓時，宋師果至，柔遮擊之，俘數百人，溺死者不可計。

translations.literal: At the second watch the Song army indeed came; Rou intercepted and struck them, capturing several hundred; those drowned were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At the second watch the Song army came as he had foreseen. Rou intercepted them, took several hundred prisoners, and drowned countless more.

sentences.zh: 攻其東門，矢石雨注，軍少卻。

translations.literal: Attacking the east gate, arrows and stones fell like rain and the army fell back somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted the east gate under a rain of arrows and stones, and the army fell back briefly.

sentences.zh: 柔率死士十餘，奮戈大呼，所向僕踣，執俘而還。

translations.literal: Rou led a dozen-odd death-defying warriors, brandishing weapons with great shouts; wherever they went men fell; they seized prisoners and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Rou led a dozen picked warriors in a furious charge, shouting as they swung their weapons. Wherever they struck men fell. They seized prisoners and fought their way back.

sentences.zh: 宋師懼，請和，乃還軍。

translations.literal: The Song army in fear sued for peace, and he thereupon withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Song army, shaken, sued for peace, and he withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 大帥察罕攻滁州，柔以二百騎往。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Chaghan attacked Chuzhou; Rou went with two hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Chaghan was besieging Chuzhou, and Rou rode to join him with two hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時盧、泗、盱眙、安豐間，宋屯戍相望，斥候甚嚴，或勸柔勿行，不聽，且戰且前，凡二十餘戰。

translations.literal: At that time between Lu, Si, Xuyi, and Anfeng Song garrisons faced one another and scouts were very strict; some urged Rou not to go, but he would not listen, fighting as he advanced through more than twenty engagements.
translations.idiomatic: Between Lu, Si, Xuyi, and Anfeng the Song had garrisons posted at every turn and scouts on strict watch. Some urged Rou not to go, but he refused to listen and fought his way forward through more than twenty engagements.

sentences.zh: 比至滁，察罕以滁久不拔，欲解去，柔請決戰，從之。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Chuzhou, Chaghan because Chuzhou long would not fall wished to withdraw; Rou requested a decisive battle and Chaghan agreed.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chuzhou, Chaghan, frustrated that the city still held, planned to withdraw. Rou asked for one decisive battle and Chaghan agreed.

sentences.zh: 既陣，宋驍將出挑戰，柔佯卻，宋將驕，柔馳及之，楇擊墜地，宋將執柔轡曳入其陣，飛石中柔鼻，兩軍哄，柔得還，裹瘡复戰。

translations.literal: Once the lines were formed a fierce Song general came out to challenge; Rou feigned retreat; the Song general grew arrogant; Rou galloped up to him, struck him down with a mace, the Song general seized Rou's reins and dragged him into their formation; a flying stone struck Rou's nose; both armies clamored; Rou got back, bound his wound, and fought again.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies were drawn up, a fierce Song champion rode out to challenge him. Rou feigned retreat. The Song man grew overconfident. Rou wheeled back, struck him down with a mace, but the Song general seized his reins and dragged him into the enemy lines. A flying stone struck Rou in the nose. Both armies erupted in uproar. Rou broke free, bound his wound, and returned to the fight.

sentences.zh: 夜遣鞏彥暉劫其營，焚城東南隅，柔率銳卒五十七人先登，拔之。

translations.literal: At night he sent Gong Yanhui to raid their camp and burn the southeast corner of the city; Rou led fifty-seven elite soldiers to mount first and took it.
translations.idiomatic: That night he sent Gong Yanhui to raid the enemy camp and burn the southeast corner of the city. Rou led fifty-seven picked warriors in the first assault over the wall and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 己亥，以本官節制河南諸翼兵馬徵行事，河南三十餘城皆屬焉。

translations.literal: On the day jihai he was given his present office to control all wing forces of Henan on campaign, and more than thirty cities of Henan came under his authority.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day he was confirmed in his present rank as commander of all wing forces of Henan on campaign, and more than thirty cities of Henan fell under his authority.

sentences.zh: 庚子，詔柔等八萬戶伐宋。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi an edict ordered Rou and others, eight ten-thousand-households, to campaign against Song.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day an edict ordered Rou and the other eight ten-thousand-household commanders to campaign against the Song.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，升保州為順天府，賜御衣數襲、名馬二、尚厩馬百。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou Baozhou was elevated to Shuntian Prefecture; he was granted several suits of imperial robes, two famous horses, and a hundred horses from the imperial stud.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou day Baozhou was elevated to Shuntian Prefecture. He received several suits of imperial robes, two famous horses, and a hundred horses from the imperial stud.

sentences.zh: 柔率師自五河口濟淮，略和州諸城，師還，分遣部下將千人屯田於襄城。

translations.literal: Rou led his army across the Huai from Wuhekou, reduced the cities of Hezhou, returned with his forces, and separately sent subordinate generals with a thousand men to garrison-farm at Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Rou led his army across the Huai at Wuhekou, reduced the cities of Hezhou, then withdrew and sent subordinate commanders with a thousand men each to establish garrison farms at Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 察罕奏柔總諸軍鎮杞。

translations.literal: Chaghan memorialized that Rou should command all armies garrisoned at Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan recommended that Rou take overall command of the armies stationed at Qi.

sentences.zh: 初，河決於汴，西南入陳留，分而為三，杞居其中潬。

translations.literal: Initially the river had burst its banks at Bian, flowed southwest into Chenliu, divided into three channels, and Qi lay amid the shallows between them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River had earlier burst its banks at Bian, flowed southwest into Chenliu, and split into three channels with Qi stranded amid the shallows between them.

sentences.zh: 宋兵恃舟楫之利，駐亳、泗，犯汴、洛，以擾河南。

translations.literal: Song troops relied on the advantage of boats, stationed at Bo and Si, and raided Bian and Luo to harass Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces exploited their naval advantage, stationed at Bo and Si, and raided Bian and Luoyang to harass Henan.

sentences.zh: 柔乃即故杞之東西中三山夾河，順殺水勢，築連城，結浮梁，為進戰退耕之計，敵不敢至。

translations.literal: Rou then took the old Qi sites of East, West, and Central Three Mountains straddling the river, followed the slowing current, built linked cities, joined floating bridges, and planned for advancing in battle and retreating to farm—the enemy did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Rou then occupied the old Qi sites at East, West, and Central Three Mountains along the river channels, followed the slackening current, built a chain of fortified towns and floating bridges, and devised a system for fighting forward and farming in retreat. The enemy dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍攻破壽州，柔欲留兵守之，察罕不從。

translations.literal: When the combined armies broke Shouzhou, Rou wished to leave troops to garrison it, but Chaghan would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: When the combined armies captured Shouzhou, Rou wanted to leave a garrison, but Chaghan refused.

sentences.zh: 又敗宋師於泗州，還杞上。

translations.literal: He again defeated the Song army at Sizhou and returned to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Song army again at Sizhou and returned to his base at Qi.

sentences.zh: 帳下吏夾谷顯祖得罪亡走，上變誣柔，執柔以北。

translations.literal: A staff officer Jiagu Xianzu offended and fled; he submitted a report slandering Rou; Rou was seized and taken north.
translations.idiomatic: A staff officer named Jiagu Xianzu offended Rou and fled. He filed a false report accusing Rou of treason, and Rou was arrested and taken north.

sentences.zh: 大臣多以闔門保柔者，卒辨其誣，顯祖伏誅。

translations.literal: Many great ministers pledged their whole households to vouch for Rou; in the end the slander was cleared, and Xianzu was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Many senior ministers pledged their households as guarantors for Rou. The charge was eventually exposed as false, and Xianzu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，憲宗即位，換授金虎符，仍軍民萬戶。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai Xianzong took the throne; Rou was reissued a golden tiger tally and remained Ten-Thousand-Household of Army and People.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Xianzong ascended the throne. Rou received a new golden tiger tally and retained his rank as Ten-Thousand-Household of Army and People.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，移鎮亳州。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin he transferred his garrison to Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day he transferred his headquarters to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 環亳皆水，非舟楫不達，柔甃城壁為橋梁屬汴堤，以通商賈之利；

translations.literal: All around Bozhou was water; without boats one could not reach it; Rou faced the city walls with brick to make bridges linking the Bian embankment, to open the profit of merchants;
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou was surrounded by water and reachable only by boat. Rou faced the city walls with brickwork to build bridges linking the Bian embankment and open the city to merchant traffic;

sentences.zh: 復建孔子廟，設校官弟子員。

translations.literal: rebuilt the Confucius temple, and established school officials and student quotas.
translations.idiomatic: rebuilt the Confucius temple, and appointed school officials with a fixed quota of students.

sentences.zh: 入奏，帝悅，賜衣一襲、翎根甲一、金符九、銀符十九，頒將校之有功者。

translations.literal: On entering audience the emperor was pleased, granted one suit of robes, one feather-root armor, nine gold tallies and nineteen silver tallies, and distributed them to meritorious officers.
translations.idiomatic: When he reported at court the emperor was pleased and granted him one suit of robes, one feather-root armor, nine gold tallies and nineteen silver tallies, which he distributed among his meritorious officers.

sentences.zh: 己未，分裨將張果、王仲仁從憲宗徵蜀；

translations.literal: On the day jiwei he detached subordinate generals Zhang Guo and Wang Zhongren to follow Xianzong in the Shu campaign;
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day he detached subordinate generals Zhang Guo and Wang Zhongren to follow Xianzong in the campaign against Shu;

sentences.zh: 王安國、胡進、田伯榮、宋演從宗王塔察兒攻荊山；

translations.literal: Wang Anguo, Hu Jin, Tian Borong, and Song Yan followed Prince Tachar in the attack on Jingshan;
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Anguo, Hu Jin, Tian Borong, and Song Yan to follow Prince Tachar in the attack on Jingshan;

sentences.zh: 柔從世祖攻鄂。

translations.literal: Rou followed Shizu in the attack on Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Rou followed Kublai Khan in the assault on Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 世祖由大勝關，柔由虎頭關，與宋兵遇於沙窩，柔子弘彥擊破之，進與守關兵戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Shizu went by Dasheng Pass, Rou by Hutou Pass; they met Song troops at Shawo; Rou's son Hongyan routed them, advanced to fight the pass garrison, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai advanced through Dasheng Pass while Rou took Hutou Pass. They met Song forces at Shawo. Rou's son Hongyan routed the enemy, then pressed forward against the pass garrison and defeated it.

sentences.zh: 世祖自陽羅渡江，促柔會兵攻鄂，百餘日不能下。

translations.literal: Shizu crossed the river from Yangluo and urged Rou to join forces in attacking Ezhou; for more than a hundred days it could not be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai crossed the Yangzi from Yangluo and pressed Rou to join the assault on Ezhou, but after more than a hundred days the city still held.

sentences.zh: 世祖諭之曰：「吾猶獵者，不能擒圈中豕，野獵以供汝食，汝可破圈而取之。」

translations.literal: Shizu instructed him: "I am like a hunter who cannot catch the pig in the pen; I hunt in the wild to supply your food—you may break the pen and take it."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai told him, "I am like a hunter who cannot catch the pig in the pen. I hunt in the wild to feed you—now break the pen and take the pig yourself."

sentences.zh: 柔乃令何伯祥作鵝車，洞掘其城，別遣勇士先登，攻其西南陬，屢破之。

translations.literal: Rou then had He Boxiang build goose carts, tunnel and undermine the walls, separately sent daring warriors to mount first, attacked the southwest corner, and repeatedly broke through.
translations.idiomatic: Rou then had He Boxiang build siege towers and tunnel under the walls. He sent picked warriors to scale the ramparts first and assaulted the southwest corner again and again until the defenses gave way.

sentences.zh: 會憲宗凶問至，宋亦行成，世祖北還，命柔統領蒙古、漢軍，以俟後命，城白鹿磯，為久駐計。

translations.literal: When news of Xianzong's death arrived, Song also sued for peace; Shizu returned north, ordered Rou to command Mongol and Han armies awaiting further orders, and fortified Bailu Rock for a long encampment.
translations.idiomatic: News of Möngke Khan's death arrived, and the Song also sued for peace. Kublai withdrew north, left Rou in command of the Mongol and Han armies to await further orders, and fortified Bailu Rock for a prolonged stay.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，詔班師。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong the Emperor Shizu took the throne and ordered the armies to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Kublai took the throne, he ordered the armies to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥反，世祖北征，詔柔入衞，至廬朐河，有詔止之。

translations.literal: Ariq Böke rebelled; Shizu campaigned north and ordered Rou to enter the guard; he reached the Luju River, where an edict stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ariq Böke rebelled, Kublai marched north and ordered Rou to come to the imperial guard. Rou reached the Luju River, but an edict recalled him.

sentences.zh: 分其兵三千五百衞京師，以子弘慶為質。

translations.literal: Three thousand five hundred of his troops were detached to guard the capital, and his son Hongqing was left as hostage.
translations.idiomatic: He detached three thousand five hundred troops to guard the capital and left his son Hongqing behind as a hostage.

sentences.zh: 二年，以金實錄獻諸朝，且請致仕，封安肅公，命第八子弘略襲職。

translations.literal: In the second year he presented the Veritable Records of Jin to the court, also requested retirement, was enfeoffed as Duke of Ansù, and his eighth son Honglue was ordered to succeed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he presented the Veritable Records of Jin to the court and asked to retire. He was enfeoffed as Duke of Ansù, and his eighth son Honglue was ordered to succeed to his office.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，加榮祿大夫，判行工部事，城大都。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing, made acting head of the Ministry of Works, and built Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan he was promoted to Grand Master of Glorious Blessing, placed in charge of the Ministry of Works, and helped build Dadu.

sentences.zh: 四年，進封蔡國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was advanced to Duke of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was advanced to Duke of Cai.

sentences.zh: 五年六月卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year he died at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the fifth year at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠宣力翊運功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國，諡武康。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted the title Merit Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Displays Strength, and Supports the Dynasty, Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with Honor Equal to the Three Councils, and Supreme Pillar of the State, with the posthumous name Wukang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title Merit Subject Who Promotes Loyalty, Displays Strength, and Supports the Dynasty, along with Grand Preceptor, Grand Master of the Palace with Honor Equal to the Three Councils, and Supreme Pillar of the State; his posthumous name was Wukang.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，加封汝南王，諡忠武。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Runan, with the posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yanyou he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Runan, with the posthumous name Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 子十有一人，弘略、弘範最顯，弘範自有傳。

translations.literal: He had eleven sons; Honglue and Hongfan were the most prominent, and Hongfan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: He had eleven sons. Honglue and Hongfan were the most prominent; Hongfan has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 弘略字仲傑，柔第八子也。

translations.literal: Honglue, style name Zhongjie, was Rou's eighth son.
translations.idiomatic: Honglue, styled Zhongjie, was Rou's eighth son.

sentences.zh: 有謀略，通經史，善騎射。

translations.literal: He had strategic ability, was versed in the classics and histories, and excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was resourceful in counsel, well versed in the classics and histories, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 嘗從柔鎮杞徙亳。

translations.literal: He once followed Rou in garrisoning Qi and moving to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He had followed his father from the garrison at Qi to Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 歲乙卯，入朝憲宗，授金符，權順天萬戶。

translations.literal: In the year yimao he entered court before Xianzong, was granted a gold tally, and made Acting Ten-Thousand-Household of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In the yimao year he attended court before Möngke Khan, received a gold tally, and was appointed acting Ten-Thousand-Household of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 從征蜀，以其幼，賜錦衣，令還鎮。

translations.literal: He followed the Shu campaign; because he was young, he was granted brocade robes and ordered to return to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Shu, but because he was still young he was given brocade robes and sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 柔既致仕，授弘略金虎符、順天路管民總管、行軍萬戶，仍總宣德、河南、懷孟等路諸軍屯亳者。

translations.literal: After Rou retired, Honglue was given a golden tiger tally, made Chief Administrator of the People of Shuntian Circuit, Military Ten-Thousand-Household, and still commanded all armies of Xuande, Henan, Huaimeng and other circuits garrisoned at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: When Rou retired, Honglue received a golden tiger tally and was appointed Chief Administrator of the People of Shuntian Circuit and Military Ten-Thousand-Household, while retaining command of all armies from Xuande, Henan, Huaimeng, and other circuits stationed at Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮反，求救於宋將夏貴。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled and sought aid from the Song general Xia Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled and appealed to the Song general Xia Gui for help.

sentences.zh: 貴自蘄乘虛北奪亳、滕、徐、宿、邳、滄、濱七州，新蔡、符離、蘄、利津四縣，殺守將。

translations.literal: Gui from Qi seized the moment to march north and take the seven prefectures of Bo, Teng, Xu, Su, Pi, Cang, and Bin, and the four counties of Xincai, Fuli, Qi, and Lijin, killing the defending officers.
translations.idiomatic: Gui advanced north from Qi while the Yuan forces were distracted and seized seven prefectures—Bo, Teng, Xu, Su, Pi, Cang, and Bin—and four counties—Xincai, Fuli, Qi, and Lijin—killing the defending officers as he went.

sentences.zh: 弘略率戰船遏之於渦口，貴退保蘄，弘略發亳軍攻之，水陸並進。

translations.literal: Honglue led war vessels to block him at Wokou; Gui retreated to defend Qi; Honglue launched the Bo army against him, advancing by land and water together.
translations.idiomatic: Honglue led his war fleet to block Gui at Wokou. Gui fell back to defend Qi. Honglue then launched the Bozhou army in a combined land and river assault.

sentences.zh: 宋兵素憚亳軍，焚城宵遁，追殺殆盡，獲軍資不可計，盡复所失地。

translations.literal: Song troops had always feared the Bo army; they burned the city and fled by night; pursuit killed nearly all; military stores captured were beyond counting; all lost territory was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: The Song troops had long feared the Bozhou army. They burned the city and fled by night. Honglue's pursuit killed nearly all of them, captured vast stores of supplies, and recovered every lost territory.

sentences.zh: 李璮既誅，追問當時與璮通書者，獨弘略書皆勸以忠義，事得釋。

translations.literal: After Li Tan was executed, they investigated those who had corresponded with Tan at the time; only Honglue's letters all urged loyalty and righteousness, and the matter was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Tan was put to death, the court investigated everyone who had corresponded with him. Honglue's letters alone had urged loyalty to the throne, and he was cleared of suspicion.

sentences.zh: 朝廷懲璮叛逆，務裁諸侯權以保全之，因解弘略兵職，宿衛京師，賜只孫冠服，以從宴享。

translations.literal: The court, punishing Tan's rebellion, sought to curtail feudatory powers for their preservation, and therefore relieved Honglue of military office, had him guard the capital, and granted him jisun court dress to attend banquets.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of Tan's rebellion the court sought to curb the power of the feudatories. Honglue was relieved of military command, assigned to guard the capital, and granted jisun court dress so he could attend imperial banquets.

sentences.zh: 至元三年，城大都，佐其父為築宮城總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhiyuan, when the capital was being built, he assisted his father as Director-General of Palace City Construction.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhiyuan, during the construction of Dadu, he assisted his father as director-general of palace-city construction.

sentences.zh: 八年，授朝列大夫、同行工部事，兼領宿衛親軍、儀鸞等局。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was made Grand Master of the Court, Associate Director of the Ministry of Works, and concurrently commanded the Palace Guard, Ceremonial Escort, and other bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Grand Master of the Court and associate director of the Ministry of Works, while also commanding the palace guard, ceremonial escort, and related bureaus.

sentences.zh: 十三年，城成，賜內帑金扣、玳瑁卮，授中奉大夫、淮東道宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, when the city was completed, he was granted gold clasps and tortoise-shell cups from the inner treasury and made Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Pacification Commissioner of Huaidong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was completed in the thirteenth year, he received gold clasps and tortoise-shell cups from the imperial treasury and was appointed Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Pacification Commissioner of Huaidong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十四年，宋廣王昺據閩、廣，時東海縣儲粟數万，行省檄弘略將兵二千戍之，仍命造舟運粟入淮安。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Song Prince of Guang, Bing, held Fujian and Guangdong; at that time Donghai County stored tens of thousands of piculs of grain; the branch secretariat ordered Honglue with two thousand troops to garrison it and also commanded him to build boats to transport grain to Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year the Song Prince of Guang, Bing, held Fujian and Guangdong. Donghai County had stored tens of thousands of piculs of grain. The branch secretariat ordered Honglue to garrison the county with two thousand men and to build boats to ship the grain to Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 弘略顧民舟，有能載粟十石者與一石，人爭趨之，一月而畢。

translations.literal: Honglue looked to civilian boats: whoever could carry ten piculs of grain received one picul; people rushed to compete; in one month it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Honglue hired civilian boats, offering one picul of grain for every ten piculs transported. People rushed to take part, and the work was finished within a month.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遷江西宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was transferred to Pacification Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 會饒州盜起，犯都昌。

translations.literal: When bandits rose in Raozhou and raided Duchang,
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Raozhou and attacked Duchang,

sentences.zh: 弘略以為，饒雖屬江東，與南康止隔一湖，此寇不滅，則吾境必有相扇而起者。

translations.literal: Honglue judged that though Raozhou belonged to Jiangdong, it was separated from Nankang by only one lake; if this band was not destroyed, his jurisdiction would surely see others stirred up in response.
translations.idiomatic: Honglue reasoned that although Raozhou lay in Jiangdong, it was separated from his jurisdiction at Nankang by only one lake. If this band were not destroyed, others in his territory would surely rise in sympathy.

sentences.zh: 乃使人直搗其巢穴，生縛賊酋，磔於市，餘黨潰散。

translations.literal: He therefore sent men straight to their nest, captured the bandit chief alive, dismembered him in the market, and the rest scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men straight to their stronghold, captured the bandit chief alive, executed him by dismemberment in the marketplace, and the rest of the gang scattered.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「不操兵者，皆為平民，餘無所問。」

translations.literal: He issued an order: "Those who did not bear arms are all civilians; nothing more will be asked."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "Anyone who did not bear arms is a civilian and will not be questioned further."

sentences.zh: 頃之，以疾歸亳。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, on account of illness he returned to Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he returned to Bozhou on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 有讒貴臣子在江南買田宅樂而忘歸者，詞引弘略。

translations.literal: Someone slandered that a noble's son had bought estates in Jiangnan and delighted in staying, forgetting to return; the accusation implicated Honglue.
translations.idiomatic: A slanderer claimed that a nobleman's son had bought estates in the south, grown content there, and forgotten to return—and implicated Honglue in the charge.

sentences.zh: 或謂弘略曰：「公但居亳，未嘗在江南，入見宜自明。」

translations.literal: Some told Honglue: "You have only dwelt at Bo and never been in Jiangnan; on entering audience you should explain yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Honglue, "You have lived only at Bozhou and never in the south. When you appear at court you should clear your name."

sentences.zh: 弘略曰：「明之，則言者獲譴矣，吾寧稱疾家居。」

translations.literal: Honglue said: "If I make it clear, the accuser will be punished; I would rather claim illness and remain at home."
translations.idiomatic: Honglue replied, "If I clear my name, the accuser will be punished. I would rather plead illness and stay at home."

sentences.zh: 二十九年，見世祖於龍虎台，請曰：「臣之子玠長矣，願備宿衛。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he saw Shizu at Longhutai and requested: "My son Jie has grown; I wish him to serve in the palace guard."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he met Kublai at Longhutai and said, "My son Jie has come of age. I ask that he serve in the palace guard."

sentences.zh: 從之，且賜以酒曰：「卿年未老，謝事何為。」

translations.literal: The emperor agreed, and moreover granted him wine, saying: "You are not yet old—why withdraw from office?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and gave him wine, saying, "You are not yet old. Why retire from office?"

sentences.zh: 特命為河南行省參知政事。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Associate Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Associate Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yuanzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yuanzhen.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠佐理功臣、銀青榮祿大夫、平章政事、上柱國、蔡國公，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Meritorious Minister for Supporting Loyalty and Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, Grand Councillor, Pillar of the State, Duke of Cai, with posthumous title Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was honored as Meritorious Minister for Supporting Loyalty and Governance, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal, Grand Councillor, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Cai, with the posthumous title Zhongyi (Loyal and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 子三人：玠，瑾，琰。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Jie, Jin, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Jie, Jin, and Yan.

sentences.zh: ○史天倪

translations.literal: ○ Shi Tianni
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shi Tianni

sentences.zh: 史天倪，字和甫，燕之永清人。

translations.literal: Shi Tianni, style name Hefu, was a native of Yongqing in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianni, styled Hefu, came from Yongqing in Yan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖倫，少好俠，因築室發土得金，始饒於財。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Lun in youth loved chivalry; while building a house he dug up gold in the earth and first became wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Lun was chivalrous in his youth. While building a house he unearthed gold and became the family's first wealthy man.

sentences.zh: 金末，中原塗炭，乃建家塾，招徠學者，所藏活豪士甚眾，以俠稱於河朔。

translations.literal: At the end of Jin, when the Central Plain was ravaged, he built a family school, attracted scholars, sheltered and aided many bold heroes, and was known for chivalry in Heshuo.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jin, when the Central Plain lay in ruins, he founded a family school, gathered scholars, sheltered many bold spirits, and was famed for chivalry throughout Heshuo.

sentences.zh: 士族陷為奴虜者，輒出金贖之。

translations.literal: When gentry families fell into slavery he would pay gold to redeem them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever gentry families fell into slavery, he paid gold to ransom them.

sentences.zh: 甲子，歲大侵，發粟八萬石賑饑者，士皆爭附之。

translations.literal: In the year jiazi there was a great famine; he distributed eighty thousand piculs of grain to relieve the hungry, and scholars all strove to attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiazi year a great famine struck. He distributed eighty thousand piculs of grain to feed the hungry, and men of learning flocked to his side.

sentences.zh: 祖成珪，倜儻有父風。

translations.literal: His grandfather Chenggui was free-spirited and had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Chenggui was free-spirited and inherited his father's bold character.

sentences.zh: 遭亂，盜賊四起，乃悉散其家財，唯存廩粟而已。

translations.literal: When disorder came and bandits rose on every side, he dispersed all his family wealth, keeping only the granary grain.
translations.idiomatic: When chaos spread and bandits rose everywhere, he gave away his entire family fortune, keeping only the grain in the granary.

sentences.zh: 父秉直，讀書尚氣義。

translations.literal: His father Bingzhi studied books and prized integrity and honor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bingzhi was a scholar who prized loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，太師、國王木華黎統兵南伐，所向殘破，秉直聚族謀曰：「方今國家喪亂，吾家百口，何以自保！」

translations.literal: In the year guiyou, Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali commanded troops south in conquest, ravaging wherever he went; Bingzhi gathered the clan and said: "Now the state is in chaos—how can our household of a hundred mouths preserve itself!"
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali led his army south, laying waste wherever he marched. Bingzhi gathered the clan and said, "The realm is in chaos. How can our household of a hundred souls survive?"

sentences.zh: 既而知降者皆得免，乃率里中老稚數千人，詣涿州軍門降。

translations.literal: Learning thereafter that those who surrendered were all spared, he led several thousand old and young of the village to the army gates at Zhuozhou to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that those who surrendered were spared, he led several thousand villagers, young and old, to the gates of the army at Zhuozhou and submitted.

sentences.zh: 木華黎欲用秉直，秉直辭而薦其子，乃以天倪為萬戶，而命秉直管領降人家屬，屯霸州。

translations.literal: Muqali wished to employ Bingzhi; Bingzhi declined and recommended his son; Tianni was made Ten-Thousand-Household, and Bingzhi was ordered to oversee the families of those who had surrendered, garrisoned at Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali wished to employ Bingzhi, but Bingzhi declined and recommended his son instead. Tianni was made Ten-Thousand-Household, and Bingzhi was assigned to oversee the families of the surrendered and garrison them at Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 秉直拊循有方，遠近聞而附者十餘萬家。

translations.literal: Bingzhi comforted and guided them with skill; more than a hundred thousand households near and far heard and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi governed them with skill and compassion. More than a hundred thousand households from near and far came to join him.

sentences.zh: 尋遷之漠北，降人道飢，秉直得所賜牛羊，悉分食之，多所全活。

translations.literal: Soon they were moved to the northern deserts; the surrendered suffered hunger; Bingzhi took the cattle and sheep granted him and divided them all for food, saving many lives.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon moved to the northern steppe. The surrendered people were starving. Bingzhi took the cattle and sheep granted him, distributed all of it for food, and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，從木華黎攻北京。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu he followed Muqali in attacking the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day he followed Muqali in the assault on the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，北京降，木華黎承製以烏野兒為北京路都元帥，秉直行尚書六部事，主饋餉，軍中未嘗乏絕。

translations.literal: On the day yihai the Northern Capital surrendered; Muqali by imperial commission made Wuyeer Grand Marshal of the Northern Capital Circuit; Bingzhi acted in the Six Ministries of the Secretariat, oversaw provisions, and the army never lacked supplies.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the Northern Capital surrendered. Muqali appointed Wuyeer Grand Marshal of the Northern Capital Circuit by imperial commission and assigned Bingzhi to the Six Ministries of the Secretariat to oversee supplies. The army never went wanting.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以老謝事，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin he resigned on account of age and returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day he retired on account of age and returned home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 三子：長天倪，次天安，次天澤。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the eldest Tianni, next Tian'an, next Tianze.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: the eldest was Tianni, the second Tian'an, and the third Tianze.

sentences.zh: 天澤自有傳。

translations.literal: Tianze has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze has his own biography elsewhere in the History.

sentences.zh: 天倪始生之夕，白氣貫庭。

translations.literal: On the night Tianni was born, white vapor pierced the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On the night Tianni was born, a white vapor pierced the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 成童，姿貌魁傑。

translations.literal: When he reached boyhood his bearing was imposing and heroic.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was tall and striking in appearance.

sentences.zh: 有道士見而異之曰：「封侯相也。」

translations.literal: A Daoist priest saw him and marveled, saying: "A count or minister he shall be."
translations.idiomatic: A Daoist priest saw him and exclaimed, "This boy is destined for rank as a marquis or minister."

sentences.zh: 及長，好學，日誦千言。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved learning and recited a thousand characters a day.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he loved learning and could recite a thousand characters a day.

sentences.zh: 大安末，舉進士不第，乃歎曰：「大丈夫立身，獨以文乎哉！

translations.literal: At the end of Da'an he sat for the jinshi examination and failed; he sighed: "Must a great man establish himself only through letters!
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Da'an era he took the jinshi examination and failed. He sighed, "Must a great man make his name through scholarship alone?

sentences.zh: 使吾遇荒雞夜鳴，擁百萬之眾，功名可唾手取也。」

translations.literal: Had I met the barren cock crowing in the night and commanded a host of a million, fame and merit could be taken at a breath."
translations.idiomatic: If the hour of chaos should come and I commanded a million men, glory would be mine for the taking."

sentences.zh: 木華黎見而奇之。

translations.literal: Muqali saw him and regarded him as extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali met him and was struck by his abilities.

sentences.zh: 既以萬戶統諸降卒，從木華黎略地三關已南，至於東海，所過城邑皆下。

translations.literal: Once made Ten-Thousand-Household commanding all surrendered troops, he followed Muqali in reducing territory south of the Three Passes as far as the Eastern Sea; every city and town passed was taken.
translations.idiomatic: As Ten-Thousand-Household commanding the surrendered troops, he followed Muqali in reducing the lands south of the Three Passes all the way to the Eastern Sea. Every city and town along the way fell to them.

sentences.zh: 因進言於木華黎曰：「金棄幽燕，遷都於汴，已失策矣。

translations.literal: He therefore advanced counsel to Muqali: "Jin has abandoned Youyan and moved the capital to Bian—this is already a mistaken policy.
translations.idiomatic: He advised Muqali, "The Jin have abandoned Youyan and moved their capital to Bian. That was already a fatal mistake.

sentences.zh: 遼水東西諸郡，金之腹心也。

translations.literal: The commanderies east and west of the Liao River are the heart of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The commanderies east and west of the Liao River are the heartland of Jin.

sentences.zh: 我若得大寧以挖其喉襟，則金雖有遼陽，終不能保矣。」

translations.literal: If we take Daning to seize their throat, then though Jin holds Liaoyang, in the end it cannot be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: If we take Daning and seize their throat, the Jin may hold Liaoyang but will never keep it."

sentences.zh: 木華黎善之。

translations.literal: Muqali approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 先，倫卒時，河朔諸郡結清樂社四十餘，社近千人，歲時像倫而祠之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Lun died, more than forty Qingle societies were formed in the commanderies of Heshuo, each society nearly a thousand strong, who yearly made his image and sacrificed to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun died, more than forty Qingle societies were formed across Heshuo, each numbering nearly a thousand members who made his image and sacrificed to him every year.

sentences.zh: 至是，天倪選其壯勇萬人為義兵，號清樂軍，以從兄天祥為先鋒，所向無敵。

translations.literal: At this time Tianni selected ten thousand of their stalwart braves as volunteer troops, titled them the Qingle Army, made his cousin Tianxiang vanguard, and they were invincible wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tianni selected ten thousand of their bravest men as volunteer troops, called them the Qingle Army, and made his cousin Tianxiang vanguard. They were invincible wherever they marched.

sentences.zh: 分兵略三河、薊州，諸寨望風款服。

translations.literal: He divided his forces to reduce Sanhe and Jizhou; all stockades submitted at the news.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to reduce Sanhe and Jizhou, and stockades everywhere submitted at the news of his approach.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，朝太祖於燕之幄殿，所陳皆奇謀至計，大稱旨，賜金符，授馬步軍都統，管領二十四萬戶。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu he attended Taizu at the tent palace in Yan; all he presented were ingenious stratagems and supreme plans, greatly pleasing the emperor, who granted a gold tally and appointed him Commander-in-Chief of Horse and Foot, overseeing two hundred forty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day he attended Taizu at the tent palace in Yan. Every plan he offered was ingenious, and the emperor was greatly pleased. He received a gold tally and was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Horse and Foot, overseeing two hundred forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 從木華黎攻高州，又從攻北京，皆不戰而克。

translations.literal: He followed Muqali in attacking Gaozhou, then followed again in attacking the Northern Capital; both were taken without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Muqali in the assault on Gaozhou and again in the attack on the Northern Capital. Both cities fell without a fight.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，授右副都元帥，改賜金虎符。

translations.literal: On the day yihai he was made Right Vice Grand Marshal and re-issued a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day he was appointed Right Vice Grand Marshal and given a new golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 奉詔南征，圍平州，金經略使乞住降。

translations.literal: By imperial command he campaigned south, besieged Pingzhou, and the Jin military commissioner Qizhu surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial command he marched south, besieged Pingzhou, and the Jin military commissioner Qizhu surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進兵真定，所屬部邑無不款附。

translations.literal: Advancing to Zhending, every subordinate district and town submitted without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Zhending, and every district and town under its jurisdiction submitted.

sentences.zh: 而真定帥武仙，固守不下，遂移軍圍大名。

translations.literal: But the Zhending commander Wu Xian held firm and would not fall, so he shifted his army to besiege Daming.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhending commander Wu Xian, however, held firm and would not yield, so Tianni shifted his army to besiege Daming.

sentences.zh: 眾謂城堅不可擊，天倪使攻其西南角，勁卒屢上屢卻，天倪先登，守者辟易，遂破其城。

translations.literal: The host said the walls were strong and could not be assaulted; Tianni had them attack the southwest corner; elite troops mounted repeatedly and were repeatedly driven back; Tianni mounted first, defenders gave way, and the city was broken.
translations.idiomatic: His men said the walls were too strong to assault. Tianni ordered an attack on the southwest corner. Elite troops climbed again and again only to be driven back, until Tianni himself scaled the wall first. The defenders gave way, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 丙子，會木華黎兵於燕南，清州監軍王守約、平州推官合達，俱以城叛，連謀越海歸金，天倪追襲至樂安，合達以益都行省忙古兵來拒，敗之，殺守約，擒忙古，斬首萬級。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi he joined Muqali's army south of Yan; the Qingzhou military inspector Wang Shouyue and Pingzhou aide Hedda both rebelled with their cities, plotting together to cross the sea and return to Jin; Tianni pursued to Le'an; Hedda with Manggu's troops of the Yidu Branch Secretariat came to resist; Tianni defeated them, killed Shouyue, captured Manggu, and beheaded ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day he joined Muqali south of Yan. Wang Shouyue, military inspector of Qingzhou, and Hedda, aide of Pingzhou, both rebelled with their cities and plotted to cross the sea back to the Jin. Tianni pursued them to Le'an. Hedda brought Manggu's troops from the Yidu branch secretariat to resist, but Tianni defeated them, killed Shouyue, captured Manggu, and took ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，徇山東諸郡，部卒有殺民豕者，立斬以徇，軍中肅然；

translations.literal: On the day dingchou he swept the commanderies of Shandong; when a soldier killed a civilian's pig he was immediately beheaded as an example, and the army became orderly;
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day he swept through the commanderies of Shandong. When a soldier killed a civilian's pig, Tianni had him beheaded on the spot as an example, and discipline was restored throughout the army.

sentences.zh: 遠近響應，知中山李明、趙州李瑀、邢州武貴、威州武振、磁州李平、洺州張立等，望風皆下。

translations.literal: near and far responded; the prefects Li Ming of Zhongshan, Li Yu of Zhao, Wu Gui of Xing, Wu Zhen of Wei, Li Ping of Ci, Zhang Li of Ming, and others all submitted at the news.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders near and far submitted at the news: Li Ming of Zhongshan, Li Yu of Zhao, Wu Gui of Xing, Wu Zhen of Wei, Li Ping of Ci, Zhang Li of Ming, and others all surrendered without a fight.

sentences.zh: 己卯，從木華黎徇河東，至絳州，其團樓甃以石，牢不可破。

translations.literal: On the day jimao he followed Muqali in sweeping Hedong, reaching Jiangzhou; its corner tower was faced with stone and could not be broken.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he followed Muqali through Hedong to Jiangzhou, whose corner tower was faced with stone and seemed impregnable.

sentences.zh: 天倪命穴其旁，地虛，樓陷，遂拔之。

translations.literal: Tianni ordered tunnels dug beside it; the ground hollowed, the tower collapsed, and it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Tianni ordered tunnels dug beside it. The ground gave way, the tower collapsed, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 木華黎喜，賞以繡衣、金鞍、名馬。

translations.literal: Muqali was pleased and rewarded him with embroidered robes, a gold saddle, and famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali was delighted and rewarded him with embroidered robes, a gold saddle, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，還軍真定，武仙降。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen he returned his army to Zhending and Wu Xian surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day he returned to Zhending, and Wu Xian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 木華黎承製以天倪為金紫光祿大夫、河北西路兵馬都元帥，行府事；

translations.literal: Muqali by imperial commission made Tianni Grand Master of Golden Purple Glory, Grand Marshal of the Western Hebei Army, acting in prefectural affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Muqali appointed Tianni Grand Master of Golden Purple Glory and Grand Marshal of the Western Hebei Army by imperial commission, entrusting him with prefectural affairs;

sentences.zh: 仙副之。

translations.literal: Xian served as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: with Wu Xian as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 天倪乃言於木華黎曰：「今中原粗定，而所過猶縱鈔掠，非王者吊民伐罪意也。

translations.literal: Tianni then said to Muqali: "Now the Central Plain is roughly settled, yet wherever we pass plunder is still permitted—this is not the intent of a king who comforts the people and punishes crime.
translations.idiomatic: Tianni then said to Muqali, "The Central Plain is roughly pacified, yet our troops still plunder wherever they march. That is not how a king who comes to comfort the people and punish the guilty should behave.

sentences.zh: 且王奉天子命，為天下除暴，豈復效其所為乎！」

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Highness bears Heaven's command to remove violence for the realm—how can you imitate their conduct!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness bears Heaven's command to rid the realm of tyranny. How can you imitate the very conduct you were sent to destroy?"

sentences.zh: 王曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The prince said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Well said."

sentences.zh: 下令：敢有剽虜者，以軍法從事。

translations.literal: He issued an order: whoever dares plunder shall be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: anyone who plunders will be dealt with under military law.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，金懷州元帥王榮、潞州元帥裴守謙、澤州太守王珍皆以城降。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Defender Wang Zhen of Zezhou all surrendered their cities.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day the Jin commanders Wang Rong of Huaizhou, Pei Shouqian of Luzhou, and Wang Zhen, defender of Zezhou, all surrendered their cities.

sentences.zh: 壬午，攻濟南水寨，破之。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he attacked the Jinan river stockade and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day he attacked the Jinan river stockade and captured it.

sentences.zh: 癸未，徇山西，遂克三關，不浹旬，定四十餘寨。

translations.literal: On the day guiwei he swept Shanxi, then took the Three Passes; in less than ten days he settled more than forty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei day he swept through Shanxi and took the Three Passes. In less than ten days he secured more than forty stockades.

sentences.zh: 兵至河衛，喜曰：「河衛者，夷門之限也。

translations.literal: When the army reached Hewei he rejoiced: "Hewei is the barrier of Yimen.
translations.idiomatic: When his army reached Hewei he rejoiced and said, "Hewei is the gateway to Yimen.

sentences.zh: 河衛既破，則夷門不能守矣。」

translations.literal: Once Hewei is broken, Yimen cannot be held."
translations.idiomatic: Once Hewei falls, Yimen cannot be held."

sentences.zh: 嚴實以兵來會，請自攻河衛，天倪曰：「合達、蒲瓦，亦勍敵也。」

translations.literal: Yan Shi came with troops to join him and asked to attack Hewei himself; Tianni said: "Hedda and Puwa are also formidable foes."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi arrived with troops to join him and asked to take Hewei himself. Tianni said, "Hedda and Puwa are formidable enemies as well."

sentences.zh: 實曰：「易與耳，保為公破之。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "They are easy opponents—I guarantee to break them for you."
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "They will be easy. I guarantee I will break them for you."

sentences.zh: 明日，實與蒲瓦兵遇於南門，合達兵自北奄至，實兵敗，竟為所執。

translations.literal: The next day Shi met Puwa's troops at the south gate; Hedda's forces suddenly arrived from the north; Shi's army was defeated and he was finally captured.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shi met Puwa's troops at the south gate. Hedda's forces swept down from the north. Shi's army was defeated and he was captured.

sentences.zh: 天倪曰：「合達以實歸汴，必以今夕。」

translations.literal: Tianni said: "Hedda will take Shi back to Bian—it must be tonight."
translations.idiomatic: Tianni said, "Hedda will escort Shi back to Bian. It must happen tonight."

sentences.zh: 急命馮存、杜必貴率壯士一千三百，伏延津柳渡。

translations.literal: He urgently ordered Feng Cun and Du Bigui to lead thirteen hundred stalwart warriors to ambush at Yanjin Willow Ford.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently ordered Feng Cun and Du Bigui to lead thirteen hundred picked warriors in ambush at Yanjin Willow Ford.

sentences.zh: 果夜縛實過延津，遇存等，與戰，敗之，實得脫歸，必貴戰死。

translations.literal: Indeed at night they bound Shi and passed Yanjin; they met Cun and others, fought, were defeated, Shi escaped and returned, and Bigui died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: That night the escort bound Shi and passed through Yanjin. They met Feng Cun's ambush, were defeated, and Shi escaped. Du Bigui died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝命天倪回軍真定。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor ordered Tianni to return his army to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the emperor ordered Tianni to return his army to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 甲申夏，大名總管彭義斌以宋兵犯河朔，天倪逆戰於恩州，義斌敗，入保大名。

translations.literal: In summer of the year jiashen, Daming prefect Peng Yibin with Song troops invaded Heshuo; Tianni met them at Enzhou; Yibin was defeated and withdrew into Daming.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the jiashen year, Peng Yibin, prefect of Daming, invaded Heshuo with Song troops. Tianni met him at Enzhou, routed him, and drove him back into Daming.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，師還，聞武仙之黨據西山腰水、鐵壁二寨以叛，天倪直搗其巢穴，盡掩殺之。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou the army returned; hearing that Wu Xian's partisans held Yaoshui and Tiebi stockades in the Western Hills in rebellion, Tianni struck straight at their nests and slaughtered them all.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day the army returned. Learning that Wu Xian's followers had rebelled and seized Yaoshui and Tiebi stockades in the Western Hills, Tianni struck their strongholds directly and slaughtered them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 仙怒，謀作亂，乃設宴邀天倪。

translations.literal: Xian in anger plotted rebellion and set a banquet to invite Tianni.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian, enraged, plotted rebellion and invited Tianni to a banquet.

sentences.zh: 有知其謀者，止天倪毋往，天倪不從，遂為仙所殺。

translations.literal: Someone who knew the plot urged Tianni not to go; Tianni would not listen and was thereupon killed by Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Someone who knew the plot warned Tianni not to go. He refused to listen and was killed by Wu Xian.

sentences.zh: 天倪之赴真定也，秉直密戒之曰：「觀武仙之辭氣，終不為我用，宜備之。」

translations.literal: When Tianni went to Zhending, Bingzhi secretly warned him: "Judging Wu Xian's words and manner, he will never truly serve us—you should guard against him."
translations.idiomatic: When Tianni set out for Zhending, Bingzhi secretly warned him, "From Wu Xian's words and manner, he will never truly serve us. You must be on your guard."

sentences.zh: 天倪曰：「我以赤心待人，人或相負，天必不容，願無慮。」

translations.literal: Tianni said: "I treat others with a loyal heart; if someone betrays me, Heaven will not permit it—have no worry."
