translations.idiomatic: Tianni replied, "I treat others with an open heart. If anyone betrays me, Heaven itself will not allow it. Have no fear."

sentences.zh: 秉直乃攜其孫楫、權還北京。

translations.literal: Bingzhi then took his grandsons Ji and Quan back to the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi then took his grandsons Ji and Quan back to the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 至是，人服其先識。

translations.literal: At this people admired his foresight.
translations.idiomatic: At that point everyone admired his foresight.

sentences.zh: 先是，天倪擊鞠夜歸，有大星隕馬前，有聲，心惡之，果及禍。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tianni returned at night from playing cuju; a great star fell before his horse with a sound; he took it as ill omen, and indeed met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Tianni was returning at night from a game of cuju, a great star fell before his horse with a loud crash. He took it as an ill omen, and disaster soon followed.

sentences.zh: 天倪死時，年三十九。

translations.literal: When Tianni died he was thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Tianni was thirty-nine when he died.

sentences.zh: 妻程氏，聞亂，恐污於賊，乃自殺。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Cheng, hearing of the turmoil, feared defilement by the rebels and killed herself.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Cheng, hearing of the upheaval, feared violation by the rebels and took her own life.

sentences.zh: 子五人，其三人尚幼，俱死於難，惟楫、權在。

translations.literal: He had five sons; three were still young and all died in the calamity; only Ji and Quan survived.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons. Three were still young and all perished in the violence. Only Ji and Quan survived.

sentences.zh: 楫字大濟。

translations.literal: Ji, style name Daji.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, styled Daji.

sentences.zh: 歲己亥，知中山府事。

translations.literal: In the year jihai he administered the affairs of Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the jihai year he was put in charge of Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋遷征南行軍萬戶翼經略，徇地蘄、黃，善撫士卒，所向有功。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Southern Campaign Military Ten-Thousand-Household Wing Commissioner, reduced Qi and Huang, treated soldiers well, and won merit wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made wing commissioner of the Southern Campaign Military Ten-Thousand-Household. He reduced Qi and Huang, treated his soldiers with care, and won success wherever he campaigned.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，天澤引楫入見太宗，奏曰：「臣兄天倪死事時，二子尚幼，臣受詔攝行府事，今楫已成人，乞解職授之。」

translations.literal: In the year renyin Tianze led Ji to audience with Taizong and memorialized: "When my brother Tianni died in service his two sons were still young; I received command to act in prefectural affairs; now Ji has come of age—I beg to resign and grant him the post."
translations.idiomatic: In the renyin year Tianze brought Ji to audience with Taizong and said, "When my brother Tianni died in service, his two sons were still children. I was ordered to act in his stead. Ji has now come of age, and I ask to resign and hand the post to him."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉歎曰：「今之爭官者多，讓官者少，卿此舉殊可嘉尚。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and sighed: "Today many contend for office, few yield office—your act is especially admirable.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him warmly. "Today everyone scrambles for office, but few yield it. Your conduct is truly admirable.

sentences.zh: 朕自有官與之。」

translations.literal: I myself have an office to give him."
translations.idiomatic: I shall grant him an office of my own."

sentences.zh: 即以楫為真定兵馬都總管，佩金虎符。

translations.literal: Ji was thereupon made Grand Commander of Zhending Army and Horse, wearing the golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was appointed Grand Commander of the Zhending army and horse and given the golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，朝廷始徵包銀，楫請以銀與物折，仍減其元數，詔從之，著為令。

translations.literal: In the year xinhai the court first levied wrapped silver; Ji requested that silver be commuted in goods and the base amount reduced; an edict approved this and it was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinhai year the court first levied the wrapped-silver tax. Ji asked that it be payable in goods as well as silver and that the base amount be reduced. The emperor approved, and the rule was written into law.

sentences.zh: 各道以楮幣相貿易，不得出境，二三歲輒一易，鈔本日耗，商旅不通，楫請立銀鈔相權法，人以為便。

translations.literal: Each circuit traded in paper notes that could not leave the circuit; every two or three years they were replaced; note capital daily dwindled and merchants could not travel; Ji requested establishing a mutual valuation law for silver and notes, and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit used paper notes for internal trade that could not cross circuit borders and were replaced every two or three years. The notes steadily lost value and commerce stalled. Ji proposed a system linking silver and paper notes by weight, which people welcomed as a practical reform.

sentences.zh: 或請運鹽按籍計口，給民以食，楫爭其不可，曰：「鹽鐵從民貿易，何可若差稅例配之。」

translations.literal: Some requested transporting salt and allocating by household registers according to population to feed the people; Ji argued this could not be done, saying: "Salt and iron follow the people's trade—how can they be assigned like corvée tax quotas."
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed distributing salt by household register to feed the people. Ji objected strongly. "Salt and iron are traded freely by the people. How can they be rationed like corvée quotas?"

sentences.zh: 議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was thereupon dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 元氏民有訴府僚於達官者，質之無實，將抵之死，楫力為營解。

translations.literal: A Yuan clan townsman accused a prefectural aide to a high official; on investigation there was no substance; he was about to be condemned to death; Ji strenuously secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman of the Yuan clan accused a prefectural aide to a high official. Investigation found no substance to the charge, yet the man was about to be executed. Ji fought hard to save him.

sentences.zh: 達官曰：「是人陷汝輩死地，而反救之，何耶？」

translations.literal: The high official said: "This man would have sent you to your deaths—why save him instead?"
translations.idiomatic: The high official said, "This man tried to send you to your deaths. Why save him?"

sentences.zh: 楫曰：「誅之固足以懲後，未若宥之以愧其心。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Executing him would indeed warn posterity, but pardoning him would better shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ji replied, "Execution would warn others, but pardon would shame him more deeply.

sentences.zh: 況人命至重，豈宜以妄言之故，而加以極刑。」

translations.literal: Moreover human life is supremely weighty—how can extreme punishment be applied for a false accusation."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, human life is precious. How can we impose the death penalty for a false accusation?"

sentences.zh: 乃杖而遣之。

translations.literal: He was flogged and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The accuser was flogged and sent away.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，授真定路總管、同判本道宣撫司事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was made Prefect of Zhending Circuit and Associate Administrator of the circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong he was appointed Prefect of Zhending Circuit and associate administrator of the circuit pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 真定表山帶河，連屬三十餘城，生殺進退，咸倚專決。

translations.literal: Zhending faced mountains and embraced rivers, linked to more than thirty cities; life and death, advance and retreat, all depended on his sole decision.
translations.idiomatic: Zhending lay among mountains and rivers, linked to more than thirty cities. Life, death, promotion, and dismissal all rested on his sole authority.

sentences.zh: 楫謹身率先，明政化，信賞罰，任賢良，汰貪墨，卹煢獨，民咸德之。

translations.literal: Ji disciplined himself and led by example, clarified government and transformation, trusted rewards and punishments, employed the worthy, removed the corrupt, relieved the solitary and bereaved, and the people all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji led by personal example, clarified policy, enforced fair rewards and punishments, employed worthy men, removed the corrupt, and cared for the destitute. The people held him in deep regard.

sentences.zh: 所舉州縣佐史有文學者三十餘人，後皆知名。

translations.literal: Of the more than thirty prefectural and county aides of literary talent he recommended, all later became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended more than thirty literate prefectural and county aides, all of whom later achieved distinction.

sentences.zh: 會天澤言：「兵民之柄不可並居一門，行之請自臣家始。」

translations.literal: When Tianze said: "Military and civil authority must not reside in one clan—let the practice begin with my family,"
translations.idiomatic: When Tianze said, "Military and civil authority must not rest in one clan. Let the reform begin with my own family,"

sentences.zh: 楫即日解綬歸。

translations.literal: Ji that same day surrendered his seal and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Ji surrendered his seal that same day and retired.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十九。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子炫，常德管軍總管；

translations.literal: His son Xuan was Garrison Commander of Changde;
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuan became garrison commander of Changde;

sentences.zh: 煇，知孟州；

translations.literal: Hui, Administrator of Mengzhou;
translations.idiomatic: Hui, administrator of Mengzhou;

sentences.zh: 燧，同知東昌府事；

translations.literal: Sui, Associate Administrator of Dongchang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Sui, associate administrator of Dongchang Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 煊，潼關提舉；

translations.literal: Xuan, Commissioner of Tongguan;
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, commissioner of Tongguan;

sentences.zh: 煬，僉廣西按察司事。

translations.literal: Yang, Secretariat Member of the Guangxi Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: and Yang, secretariat member of the Guangxi Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 權字伯衡，勇而有謀。

translations.literal: Quan, style name Boheng, was brave and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Quan, styled Boheng, was brave and resourceful in counsel.

sentences.zh: 初，以權萬戶從天澤南征。

translations.literal: Initially, as Quan Ten-Thousand-Household he followed Tianze in the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He first followed Tianze south as Quan Ten-Thousand-Household.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子，天澤以萬戶改河南經略使，乃以權代其任。

translations.literal: In the year renzi Tianze changed from Ten-Thousand-Household to Henan Military Commissioner; Quan was made to replace him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the renzi year Tianze was promoted from Ten-Thousand-Household to Henan Military Commissioner, and Quan took over his former duties.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，屯軍鄧州，敗宋將高達於樊城。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin he garrisoned Dengzhou and defeated the Song general Gao Da at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day he garrisoned Dengzhou and defeated the Song general Gao Da at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 己未，世祖自將伐宋，權出迎於淮西。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei Shizu personally led the campaign against Song; Quan went out to welcome him west of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day Kublai personally led the campaign against the Song, and Quan went out to welcome him west of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 世祖渡江，次鄂州而憲宗崩，世祖北還，乃命權總兵鎮江北岸之武磯山。

translations.literal: Shizu crossed the river, halted at Ezhou when Xianzong died, returned north, and ordered Quan to command troops garrisoning Wuji Mountain on the north bank of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai crossed the Yangzi and halted at Ezhou when Möngke Khan died. On his return north he left Quan in command of troops garrisoning Wuji Mountain on the northern bank.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，降詔獎諭，賜金虎符，授真定河間濱棣邢洺衛輝等州路並木烈糺軍兼屯田州城民戶沿邊鎮守諸軍總管萬戶；

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong an edict commended him, granted a golden tiger tally, and appointed him Grand Ten-Thousand-Household Commander of the circuits of Zhending, Hejian, Bin, Di, Xing, Ming, Weihui and others, together with the Mielie jiu army, garrison-farmers, urban households, and all frontier garrison forces;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong an edict commended him and granted a golden tiger tally. He was appointed Grand Ten-Thousand-Household Commander over the circuits of Zhending, Hejian, Bin, Di, Xing, Ming, Weihui, and others, together with the Mielie jiu army, garrison farmers, urban households, and all frontier garrison forces;

sentences.zh: 其所屬千戶、萬戶，悉聽號令。

translations.literal: all subordinate thousand- and ten-thousand-households were subject to his command.
translations.idiomatic: and all subordinate thousand- and ten-thousand-household commanders were placed under his orders.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，召至闕下，問以征南之策。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was summoned to court and asked for strategy on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was summoned to court and asked for his strategy on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「襄陽乃江陵之籓蔽，樊城乃襄陽之外郛，我軍若先攻樊城，則襄陽不能支梧，不戰自降矣。

translations.literal: He replied: "Xiangyang is the screen of Jiangling; Fancheng is the outer wall of Xiangyang—if our army first attacks Fancheng, Xiangyang cannot brace itself and will surrender without battle.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Xiangyang is the shield of Jiangling, and Fancheng is its outer defense. If we take Fancheng first, Xiangyang cannot hold and will surrender without a fight.

sentences.zh: 然後駐兵嘉定，耀武淮、泗，事必有濟。」

translations.literal: Then station troops at Jiading and display might on the Huai and Si—the affair will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Then station troops at Jiading and display our strength on the Huai and Si. The campaign will surely succeed."

sentences.zh: 帝善其計。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan.

sentences.zh: 七年，宋兵侵邊，權引兵趨荊子口，大破之，帝賜白金五百兩，權悉以分勞士卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Song troops raided the frontier; Quan led troops to Jingzikou and routed them utterly; the emperor granted five hundred taels of white silver, which Quan entirely distributed to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Song forces raided the frontier. Quan marched to Jingzikou and won a crushing victory. The emperor granted him five hundred taels of silver, which he distributed entirely among his troops.

sentences.zh: 宋將夏貴以船萬艘載壯士，欲奪江面，權進攻，破之，帝賜以衣幣、弓矢、鞍勒。

translations.literal: The Song general Xia Gui with ten thousand vessels carrying stalwart warriors wished to seize control of the river surface; Quan attacked and broke them; the emperor granted robes, silks, bows, arrows, and saddlery.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Xia Gui brought ten thousand ships loaded with picked warriors to seize the river. Quan attacked and defeated him. The emperor rewarded him with robes, silks, bows, arrows, and saddlery.

sentences.zh: 既而轉糧於隨，貴復引兵扼我前路，權戰破之，賜白金七百兩。

translations.literal: Thereafter while transporting grain at Sui, Gui again led troops to block their advance route; Quan fought and defeated him, and was granted seven hundred taels of white silver.
translations.idiomatic: While transporting grain at Sui, Gui again blocked the route ahead. Quan defeated him in battle and received seven hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 制授河南等路宣撫使，未上，賜金虎符，充江漢大都督，總制軍馬，總管屯田萬戶。

translations.literal: By appointment he was made Pacification Commissioner of Henan and other circuits; before taking office he was granted a golden tiger tally, made Grand Governor of the Jiang and Han, overall controller of army and horse, and Grand Ten-Thousand-Household of garrison farms.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Henan and other circuits. Before taking office he received a golden tiger tally and was made Grand Governor of the Jiang and Han, overall controller of armies, and Grand Ten-Thousand-Household of garrison farms.

sentences.zh: 會天澤言一門不可兼掌兵民之柄，乃授權鎮國上將軍、真定等路總管，兼府尹。

translations.literal: When Tianze said one clan must not hold both military and civil authority, Quan was made State-Securing General-in-Chief, Prefect of Zhending and other circuits, concurrently Prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianze argued that one clan must not hold both military and civil power, Quan was appointed State-Securing General-in-Chief, Prefect of Zhending and other circuits, and concurrently Prefect of the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 徙東平，又徙河間。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Dongping, then to Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Dongping and later to Hejian.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 樞字子明。

translations.literal: Shu, style name Ziming.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Ziming.

sentences.zh: 父天安，字全甫，秉直仲子也。

translations.literal: His father Tian'an, style name Quanfu, was Bingzhi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tian'an, styled Quanfu, was the second son of Bingzhi.

sentences.zh: 歲癸酉，從秉直降。

translations.literal: In the year guiyou he followed Bingzhi in surrendering.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year he followed Bingzhi in surrendering to the Mongols.

sentences.zh: 太師木華黎以其兄天倪為萬戶，而質天安軍中。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Muqali made his elder brother Tianni Ten-Thousand-Household and kept Tian'an as hostage in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Muqali made his elder brother Tianni Ten-Thousand-Household and kept Tian'an as a hostage in the army.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，從討錦州叛人張致，平之。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou he followed in suppressing the Jinzhou rebel Zhang Zhi and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day he joined the campaign against the Jinzhou rebel Zhang Zhi and pacified the region.

sentences.zh: 己卯，從略地關右，生擒鄜州驍將張資祿號張鐵槍者。

translations.literal: On the day jimao he followed in reducing territory west of the passes and captured alive the Fuzhou fierce general Zhang Zilu, called Zhang Iron Spear.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he campaigned west of the passes and captured alive Zhang Zilu of Fuzhou, known as Zhang Iron Spear.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，武仙殺天倪於真定，天安率眾來會天澤，並力攻仙，敗走之。

translations.literal: On the day yiyou Wu Xian killed Tianni at Zhending; Tian'an led his host to join Tianze, combined forces to attack Xian, and drove him off in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Wu Xian murdered Tianni at Zhending. Tian'an rallied his men to join Tianze, and together they attacked Wu Xian and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 以功授行北京元帥府事，撫治真定。

translations.literal: For his merit he was appointed to act in the Northern Capital Marshal's headquarters and pacify Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed to the Northern Capital marshal's headquarters and entrusted with governing Zhending.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，宋聚兵邢之西山，聲言為仙援，遣其徒趙和行間城中，誣倅副李甲、劉清嘗輸款為內應。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin Song gathered troops on the western hills of Xing, claiming to aid Xian, and sent their agent Zhao He to infiltrate the city, slandering deputies Li Jia and Liu Qing as having once offered surrender as inside collaborators.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day the Song massed troops on the western hills of Xing, claiming to aid Wu Xian. They sent an agent named Zhao He to infiltrate the city and accuse the deputies Li Jia and Liu Qing of having secretly offered to collaborate.

sentences.zh: 守將械兩人送府，大帥趣命戮之，天安揣知其詐，請自鞫之，果得其情，遂斬和以徇。

translations.literal: The defending general shackled the two and sent them to headquarters; the grand marshal urgently ordered execution; Tian'an sensed the fraud, requested to interrogate himself, indeed obtained the truth, and beheaded He as an example.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general arrested the two men and sent them to headquarters. The grand marshal ordered their immediate execution. Tian'an sensed a trick, asked to interrogate them himself, uncovered the plot, and executed Zhao He as a warning.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從伐金。

translations.literal: On the day renchen he followed in the campaign against Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day he joined the campaign against Jin.

sentences.zh: 師還，討劇盜梁滿、蘇杰等，悉平之。

translations.literal: When the army returned he suppressed the fierce bandits Liang Man, Su Jie, and others, pacifying them all.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he suppressed the fierce bandits Liang Man, Su Jie, and others and pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 甲午，宣權真定等路萬戶，賜金符。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu he was proclaimed Quan Ten-Thousand-Household of Zhending and other circuits and granted a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu day he was confirmed as Quan Ten-Thousand-Household of Zhending and other circuits and granted a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 丙午，入覲，賜黃金五十兩、白狐裘一、牝馬百。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu he entered audience and was granted fifty taels of gold, one white fox fur coat, and a hundred brood mares.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu day he attended court and received fifty taels of gold, one white fox-fur coat, and a hundred brood mares.

sentences.zh: 乙卯卒。

translations.literal: He died on the day yimao.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the yimao year.

sentences.zh: 樞年二十餘，以勳臣子知中山府，有治績。

translations.literal: Shu in his twenties, as son of a meritorious minister, administered Zhongshan Prefecture with governing achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties Shu, as the son of a meritorious minister, governed Zhongshan Prefecture with notable success.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，初籍新軍，天澤以長兄二子各有官位，而仲兄之子未仕，乃奏樞為徵行萬戶，配以真定、彰德、衛州、懷孟新軍，戍唐、鄧。

translations.literal: On the day jiayin when new armies were first registered, Tianze because the eldest brother's two sons each had offices while the middle brother's son had none, memorialized Shu as Campaigning Ten-Thousand-Household, paired with new armies of Zhending, Zhangde, Weizhou, and Huaimeng, garrisoned at Tang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day, when new armies were first registered, Tianze noted that the eldest brother's two sons already held office while the middle brother's son did not. He recommended Shu as Campaigning Ten-Thousand-Household with new armies from Zhending, Zhangde, Weizhou, and Huaimeng to garrison Tang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，敗宋舟師於漢水之鴛鴦灘，賜金虎符。

translations.literal: On the day yimao he defeated Song river forces at Mandarin Duck Beach on the Han River and was granted a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he defeated a Song fleet at Mandarin Duck Beach on the Han River and received a golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 戊午，憲宗伐宋，入自蜀，從天澤詣行在，朝帝於大散關。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu Xianzong campaigned against Song, entering from Shu; Shu followed Tianze to the imperial camp and attended the emperor at Dasan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day Möngke Khan campaigned against the Song through Shu. Shu followed Tianze to the imperial camp and attended the emperor at Dasan Pass.

sentences.zh: 帝勞之曰：「卿久鎮東方，茲复遠來，勤亦至矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him: "You have long garrisoned the east; now you come again from afar—your diligence is utmost."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed him, saying, "You have long guarded the east. To come so far again shows exceptional devotion."

sentences.zh: 樞對曰：「臣之祖、父，受國厚恩，今陛下親禦六師，暴露萬里之外，臣獨不能出死力，以報萬分之一邪！」

translations.literal: Shu replied: "My grandfather and father received the state's deep grace; now Your Majesty personally leads the six armies, exposed ten thousand li away—how can I alone not give my utmost strength to repay the least fraction!"
translations.idiomatic: Shu replied, "My grandfather and father received the state's deepest favors. Now Your Majesty leads the armies in person, ten thousand li from home. How can I fail to give my life in return, even for the smallest fraction of that debt?"

sentences.zh: 帝壯其言，命為前鋒。

translations.literal: The emperor was impressed by his words and ordered him as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved by his words and made him vanguard commander.

sentences.zh: 宋立劍州，僑治於苦竹崖，前阻絕澗，深數百尺，恃險而不備，帝使樞偵之。

translations.literal: Song established Jianzhou with a refugee government at Kuzhu Cliff, fronted by an impassable ravine hundreds of feet deep; relying on the peril they were unprepared; the emperor had Shu reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had established Jianzhou with a refugee government at Kuzhu Cliff, fronted by a ravine hundreds of feet deep. Trusting the terrain, they were unprepared. The emperor sent Shu to scout the position.

sentences.zh: 樞率健卒數十，縋而下，得其所以致師處以聞，帝趣樞急取之，宋人懼，乃降。

translations.literal: Shu led several dozen elite soldiers, lowered themselves on ropes, discovered where troops could be brought up and reported; the emperor urged Shu to take it quickly; the Song in fear thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shu led several dozen picked men down the cliff on ropes, found the route by which troops could be brought up, and reported back. The emperor ordered him to take the position at once. The Song, terrified, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 翼日，大宴，帝顧皇后，命飲樞酒，且諭新附渠帥曰：「我國家自開創以來，未有皇后賜臣下酒者，特以樞父子世篤忠貞，故寵以殊禮。

translations.literal: The next day at a great banquet the emperor turned to the empress and ordered her to offer Shu wine, and told the newly submitted chieftains: "Since our state's founding there has never been an empress granting wine to a minister—this is solely because the Shu father and son for generations have been deeply loyal, and so are honored with special rites.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at a great banquet the emperor turned to the empress and had her offer Shu wine. He told the newly submitted chieftains, "Since the founding of our state no empress has ever offered wine to a subject. The Shu family has been loyal for generations, and so they are honored with this exceptional rite.

sentences.zh: 有能盡瘁事國者，禮亦如之。」

translations.literal: Whoever can exhaust themselves in serving the state shall receive rites like this as well."
translations.idiomatic: Whoever serves the state with equal devotion shall receive the same honor."

sentences.zh: 己未，從天澤擊敗宋將呂文德於嘉陵江，追至重慶而還，賜黃金五十兩、白金二百兩、錦一匹。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei he followed Tianze in defeating the Song general Lü Wende on the Jialing River, pursued to Chongqing and returned, and was granted fifty taels of gold, two hundred taels of white silver, and one length of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day he followed Tianze in defeating the Song general Lü Wende on the Jialing River and pursued as far as Chongqing before returning. He received fifty taels of gold, two hundred taels of silver, and one length of brocade.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，改賜金虎符。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne he was re-issued a golden tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai ascended the throne he received a new golden tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，從天澤扈駕北征。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he followed Tianze in escorting the emperor on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he accompanied Tianze on the emperor's northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，李璮叛據濟南，復從天澤往討之。

translations.literal: In the third year Li Tan rebelled and held Jinan; he again followed Tianze to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Tan rebelled and seized Jinan. Shu again followed Tianze to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 城西南有大澗，亙歷山，樞一軍獨當其險，夾澗而城，豎木柵於澗中。

translations.literal: Southwest of the city was a great ravine spanning the mountains; Shu's army alone held the perilous point, built a city flanking the ravine, and erected wooden palisades in the ravine.
translations.idiomatic: Southwest of the city a great ravine ran through the hills. Shu's army alone held the dangerous ground, built a camp on both sides of the ravine, and set wooden palisades in the streambed.

sentences.zh: 淫雨暴漲，木柵盡壞，樞曰：「賊乘吾隙，俟夜必出。」

translations.literal: Torrential rain swelled violently, the wooden palisades were all destroyed; Shu said: "The rebels will seize our gap—they will surely come out at night."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains swelled the stream and destroyed the palisades. Shu said, "The rebels will exploit our weakness. They will attack tonight."

sentences.zh: 命作葦炬數百置城上。

translations.literal: He ordered several hundred reed torches made and placed on the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered several hundred reed torches prepared and placed along the walls.

sentences.zh: 逮三鼓，賊果至，飛炬擲之，風怒火烈，弓弩齊發，賊眾大潰，自相蹂躪，死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: By the third watch the rebels indeed came; flying torches were cast at them, wind fanned fierce flames, bows and crossbows fired together, the rebel host collapsed utterly, trampling one another, dead beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At the third watch the rebels came as he had foreseen. His men hurled the torches down. Wind fanned the flames, and bows and crossbows fired together. The rebel army broke in panic, trampling one another to death in numbers beyond count.

sentences.zh: 未幾，璮就擒。

translations.literal: Before long Tan was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Li Tan was captured.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，宋兵圍開、達諸州，以樞為左壁總帥，佩虎符，凡河南、山東、懷孟、平陽、太原、京兆、延安等軍悉統之，宋兵聞之，解去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan Song troops besieged Kai, Da, and other prefectures; Shu was made Left Wing Commander-in-Chief, wore the tiger tally, and all armies of Henan, Shandong, Huaimeng, Pingyang, Taiyuan, Jingzhao, Yan'an and others were placed under his command; hearing this, Song troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan Song forces besieged Kai, Da, and other prefectures. Shu was made Left Wing Commander-in-Chief with the tiger tally, commanding all armies of Henan, Shandong, Huaimeng, Pingyang, Taiyuan, Jingzhao, Yan'an, and other regions. At the news the Song forces withdrew.

sentences.zh: 六年，高麗人金通精據珍島以叛，討之，歲餘不下。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the Korean Jin Tongjing held Zhen Island in rebellion; they campaigned against him for more than a year without success.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Korean Jin Tongjing rebelled and seized Zhen Island. The campaign against him lasted more than a year without success.

sentences.zh: 七年，進樞昭勇大將軍、鳳州經略使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shu was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor and Military Commissioner of Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Shu was promoted to Grand General of Manifest Valor and Military Commissioner of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 樞至，謂諸將佐曰：「賊勢方張，未易力勝，況炎暑海氣蒸鬱，弓力馳弱，猝不可用。

translations.literal: When Shu arrived he told the generals and aides: "The rebels' power is just expanding—not easy to overcome by force; moreover the hot summer and steaming sea air weaken bow strength, which cannot be used in haste.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu arrived he told his officers, "The rebels are at the height of their power and cannot be beaten by force alone. The summer heat and humid sea air have weakened our bows—they are not fit for a hasty assault.

sentences.zh: 宜分軍為三，多張旗幟以疑之。

translations.literal: We should divide the army in three and display many banners to confuse them.
translations.idiomatic: Divide the army into three detachments and display many banners to confuse them.

sentences.zh: 吾與諸君潛師搗其巢穴，破之必矣。」

translations.literal: I with you shall secretly strike their nest—their defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: You and I will strike their stronghold by surprise. Victory is certain."

sentences.zh: 與戰，大破之，其地悉平。

translations.literal: They fought and routed them utterly; the whole region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They fought and won a crushing victory. The entire region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 十二年，復以萬戶從丞相伯顏伐宋，賜錦衣一、寶鞍一、弓一、矢百、甲十注、馬十二匹，仍給天澤帳下士十人以從。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he again followed Chancellor Bayan as Ten-Thousand-Household in the campaign against Song; he was granted one brocade robe, one precious saddle, one bow, a hundred arrows, ten suits of armor, twelve horses, and ten men from Tianze's staff to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he again followed Chancellor Bayan against the Song as Ten-Thousand-Household. He received a brocade robe, a precious saddle, a bow, a hundred arrows, ten suits of armor, twelve horses, and ten men from Tianze's staff to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 宋平，署安吉州安撫使。

translations.literal: When Song was pacified he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Anji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song surrender he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Anji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時新附之初，民所在依險阻自保，樞以威信招懷之，復業為民者以千萬計。

translations.literal: At that time, just after the new submission, the people everywhere relied on perilous terrain to protect themselves; Shu with prestige and trust won them over, and those who resumed livelihood as civilians numbered in the tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first days after submission the people everywhere held to mountain strongholds for protection. Shu won them over with his reputation and trust, and tens of millions returned to civilian life.

sentences.zh: 十四年，移疾還。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he returned on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he returned home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 十九年，起為東京路總管，辭不赴。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was recalled as Prefect of the Eastern Capital Circuit but declined to take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was recalled as Prefect of the Eastern Capital Circuit but declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，拜中奉大夫、山東東西道宣慰使，治濟南，後又治益都。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was made Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Shandong Circuits, governing Jinan and later Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was appointed Grand Master for Fostering Integrity and Pacification Commissioner of the Eastern and Western Shandong Circuits, first governing Jinan and later Yidu.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-fourth year at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子煥，昭勇大將軍、後衛親軍都指揮使，佩金虎符；

translations.literal: His son Huan was Grand General of Manifest Valor and Commander of the Rear Guard Palace Army, wearing the golden tiger tally;
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan became Grand General of Manifest Valor and Commander of the Rear Guard Palace Army, bearing the golden tiger tally;

sentences.zh: 燁，奉訓大夫、祕書少監。

translations.literal: Ye, Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and Ye, Grand Master for Fostering Instruction and Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: ○史天祥

translations.literal: ○ Shi Tianxiang
translations.idiomatic: ○ Shi Tianxiang

sentences.zh: 史天祥，父懷德，尚書秉直之弟也。

translations.literal: Shi Tianxiang; his father Huaide was the younger brother of Secretariat Member Bingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianxiang's father Huaide was the younger brother of Secretariat Member Bingzhi.

sentences.zh: 歲癸酉，太師、國王木華黎從太祖伐金，天祥隨秉直迎降於涿。

translations.literal: In the year guiyou Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali followed Taizu in the campaign against Jin; Tianxiang followed Bingzhi in welcoming surrender at Zhuo.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year Grand Preceptor and Prince Muqali followed Taizu in the campaign against Jin. Tianxiang accompanied Bingzhi in submitting at Zhuo.

sentences.zh: 木華黎命懷德就領其黑軍隸帳下，署天祥都鎮撫，選降卒長身武勇者二百人，使領之。

translations.literal: Muqali ordered Huaide to take command of his Black Army under the headquarters, appointed Tianxiang Chief Pacification Commissioner, selected two hundred surrendered soldiers tall and brave in war, and had him lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali placed Huaide in command of the Black Army under his headquarters and appointed Tianxiang Chief Pacification Commissioner. He selected two hundred tall, brave surrendered soldiers for Tianxiang to command.

sentences.zh: 招徠丁壯，得眾萬餘，從取霸州、文安、大城、滄濱、長山等二十餘城，東下淄、沂、密三州，所至皆先登，詔賜以銀符。

translations.literal: He recruited able-bodied men and obtained more than ten thousand followers; he followed in taking Bazhou, Wen'an, Dacheng, Cangbin, Changshan, and more than twenty cities; marched east to reduce Zi, Yi, and Mi; wherever he went he mounted first; an edict granted him a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited able-bodied men until his force exceeded ten thousand. He helped capture more than twenty cities including Bazhou, Wen'an, Dacheng, Cangbin, and Changshan, then marched east to reduce Zi, Yi, and Mi. He was always first over the wall. The court granted him a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 從大軍攻燕，不克。

translations.literal: He followed the great army in attacking Yan but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the main army in the assault on Yan but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，略地高州，拔惠和、金源、和眾、龍山、利、建、富庶等十五城，惟大寧固守不下。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu he reduced territory in Gaozhou, took Huihe, Jinyuan, Hezhong, Longshan, Li, Jian, Fushu, and fifteen other cities; only Daning held firm and would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day he campaigned in Gaozhou and took fifteen cities including Huihe, Jinyuan, Hezhong, Longshan, Li, Jian, and Fushu. Only Daning held out.

sentences.zh: 天祥獲金將完顏胡速，木華黎欲殺之，天祥曰：「殺一人無損於敵，適驅天下之人為吾敵也。

translations.literal: Tianxiang captured the Jin general Wanyan Husu; Muqali wished to kill him; Tianxiang said: "Killing one man does not harm the enemy—it only drives all under Heaven to become our enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang captured the Jin general Wanyan Husu. Muqali wished to execute him, but Tianxiang said, "Killing one man does nothing to harm the enemy. It only turns all under Heaven against us.

sentences.zh: 且其降時嘗許以不死，今殺之，無以取信於後，不若從而用之。」

translations.literal: Moreover when he surrendered we once promised he would not die—now to kill him cannot win trust hereafter; better to accept and employ him."
translations.idiomatic: Besides, we promised him his life when he surrendered. To kill him now would destroy our credibility. Better to accept him and put him to use."

sentences.zh: 乃以為千戶。

translations.literal: He was therefore made Thousand-Household.
translations.idiomatic: Husu was made Thousand-Household.

sentences.zh: 復合眾攻其城，懷德先登，擒其二將，為流矢所中，歿於軍。

translations.literal: They again combined forces to attack the city; Huaide mounted first, captured two of their generals, was struck by a stray arrow, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked the city again. Huaide scaled the wall first and captured two enemy generals, but a stray arrow struck him and he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 乃以所統黑軍命天祥領之。

translations.literal: The Black Army he had commanded was then entrusted to Tianxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Command of the Black Army then passed to Tianxiang.

sentences.zh: 天祥憤痛其父之死，攻之愈急。

translations.literal: Tianxiang in grief and rage over his father's death pressed the attack ever harder.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving his father's death, Tianxiang pressed the assault with redoubled fury.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，與大帥烏野兒降其北京留守銀答忽、同知烏古倫。

translations.literal: On the day yihai with Grand Marshal Wuyeer he received the surrender of the Northern Capital Garrison Commander Yindahu and Vice Administrator Wugulun.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day he and Grand Marshal Wuyeer accepted the surrender of the Northern Capital Garrison Commander Yindahu and Vice Administrator Wugulun.

sentences.zh: 進攻北京傍近諸寨，磨雲山王都統首詣軍門降，天祥命入列崖，擒都統不剌，釋其縛，仍曉以大義，不剌感泣，願效死。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack stockades near the Northern Capital, Commander Wang of Moyun Mountain was first to come to the army gates and surrender; Tianxiang ordered entry into Lieya Cliff, captured Commander Bula, released his bonds, still explained the great principle; Bula wept in gratitude and wished to die in service.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the stockades near the Northern Capital. Commander Wang of Moyun Mountain was the first to surrender at the gates. Tianxiang sent men into Lieya Cliff, captured Commander Bula, released him, and explained the larger cause. Bula wept and pledged his life to the cause.

sentences.zh: 天祥察其誠，許與王都統往說降城子崖王家奴，乃命三人各將舊卒，付空名告身，使諭樓子崖等二十餘寨，悉降，得老幼數万、勝兵八千。

translations.literal: Tianxiang perceived his sincerity, permitted him with Commander Wang to go persuade Chengziya's Wang Jianu to surrender; he then ordered the three each to lead their old troops, gave blank appointment documents, and had them announce to Louziya and more than twenty stockades—all submitted, obtaining tens of thousands of old and young and eight thousand fit soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Bula's sincerity, Tianxiang allowed him and Commander Wang to persuade Wang Jianu at Chengziya to surrender. He sent the three men with their old troops and blank appointment documents to announce terms to Louziya and more than twenty stockades. All submitted, yielding tens of thousands of civilians and eight thousand fighting men.

sentences.zh: 西乾河答魯、五指山楊趙奴獨固守不下，天祥擊之，大小百餘戰，趙奴死，答魯敗走，得戶二萬。

translations.literal: Xiganhe's Dalu and Wuzhishan's Yang Zhaonu alone held firm and would not fall; Tianxiang attacked them in more than a hundred engagements large and small; Zhaonu died, Dalu fled in defeat, and twenty thousand households were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Dalu of Xiganhe and Yang Zhaonu of Wuzhishan alone held out. Tianxiang fought them in more than a hundred engagements. Zhaonu was killed, Dalu fled in defeat, and twenty thousand households were secured.

sentences.zh: 授西山總帥兵馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Western Hills army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of the Western Hills armies.

sentences.zh: 興州節度使趙守玉反，天祥與烏野兒分道討平之。

translations.literal: The Xingzhou Military Commissioner Zhao Shouyu rebelled; Tianxiang and Wuyeer by separate routes suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shouyu, Military Commissioner of Xingzhou, rebelled. Tianxiang and Wuyeer suppressed him by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 答魯复聚眾攻龍山，以槊刺烏野兒中胸，隨墮馬，天祥馳救得免，复整陣出戰，大敗之，斬首八千級，答魯戰死。

translations.literal: Dalu again gathered troops to attack Longshan, speared Wuyeer in the chest, who fell from his horse; Tianxiang galloped to rescue and saved him, reformed the lines and fought again, routed them utterly, beheaded eight thousand, and Dalu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Dalu rallied his forces again and attacked Longshan, spearing Wuyeer in the chest and knocking him from his horse. Tianxiang galloped to his rescue. Reforming the lines, they fought again and won a crushing victory, taking eight thousand heads. Dalu died in the battle.

sentences.zh: 進克中興府。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Zhongxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and captured Zhongxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 張致盜據錦州，從木華黎討平之。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhi seized Jinzhou as a bandit; he followed Muqali in suppressing and pacifying him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Zhang Zhi seized Jinzhou. Tianxiang followed Muqali in suppressing him.

sentences.zh: 會契丹漢軍擒關肅，復利州，殺劉祿於銀治，斬首五十級，尖山、香爐、紅螺、塔山、大蟲、駱駝、團崖諸寨悉平，虜生口萬餘，得錦州舊將杜節，並黑軍五百人，即命統之。

translations.literal: When Khitan and Han armies captured Guan Su, recovered Lizhou, killed Liu Lu at Yinzhi with fifty heads taken, Jianshan, Xianglu, Hongluo, Tashan, Dachong, Luotuo, Tuanya and other stockades were all pacified, more than ten thousand captives taken, the old Jinzhou general Du Jie obtained together with five hundred Black Army troops, whom he immediately ordered to command.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan and Han forces captured Guan Su and recovered Lizhou, Liu Lu was killed at Yinzhi and fifty heads were taken. Stockades at Jianshan, Xianglu, Hongluo, Tashan, Dachong, Luotuo, Tuanya, and elsewhere were all pacified. More than ten thousand captives were taken. The former Jinzhou general Du Jie and five hundred Black Army troops were placed under Tianxiang's command.

sentences.zh: 丙子春，覲太祖於魚兒濼，賜金符，授提控元帥。

translations.literal: In spring of the year bingzi he attended Taizu at Yueripo, was granted a gold tally, and appointed Control Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the bingzi year he attended Taizu at Yueripo, received a gold tally, and was appointed Control Marshal.

sentences.zh: 拔蓋、金、蘇、復等州，獲金完顏奴、耶律神都馬，遷鎮國上將軍、利州節度使、所部降民都總官、監軍兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: He took Gai, Jin, Su, Fu and other prefectures, captured the Jin Wanyan Nu and Yelü Shenduma, and was transferred to State-Securing General-in-Chief, Military Commissioner of Lizhou, Chief Overseer of surrendered people under his command, and Overseer Marshal of army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the prefectures of Gai, Jin, Su, Fu, and others, and took the Jin generals Wanyan Nu and Yelü Shenduma. He was promoted to State-Securing General-in-Chief, Military Commissioner of Lizhou, Chief Overseer of the surrendered people under his command, and Overseer Marshal of armies.

sentences.zh: 丁丑夏，山賊祁和尚據武平，討平之。

translations.literal: In summer of the year dingchou the mountain bandit Qi Heshang held Wuping; he campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the dingchou year the mountain bandit Qi Heshang seized Wuping. Tianxiang suppressed him.

sentences.zh: 縛金將巢元帥。

translations.literal: He bound the Jin general Chao Yuanshuai.
translations.idiomatic: He captured the Jin general Chao Yuanshuai.

sentences.zh: 又滅重兒盜眾萬人於興州之車河。

translations.literal: He also destroyed the band of Chong'er numbering ten thousand at Chehe in Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also destroyed the ten-thousand-strong band of Chong'er at Chehe in Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 己卯，權兵馬都元帥，蒙古、漢軍、黑軍並聽節制。

translations.literal: On the day jimao he was made Acting Grand Marshal of army and horse; Mongol, Han, and Black armies all obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day he was made Acting Grand Marshal of army and horse, with Mongol, Han, and Black armies all under his command.

sentences.zh: 下河東、平陽、河中、岢嵐、絳、石、隰、吉、廓等八十餘城。

translations.literal: He reduced more than eighty cities of Hedong, Pingyang, Hezhong, Kelan, Jiang, Shi, Xi, Ji, Kuo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced more than eighty cities in Hedong, Pingyang, Hezhong, Kelan, Jiang, Shi, Xi, Ji, Kuo, and other regions.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，至真定，木華黎使天祥攻城，天祥因請曰：「攻之恐戮及無辜，不如先往諭之。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen he reached Zhending; Muqali had Tianxiang attack the city; Tianxiang therefore requested: "In attacking we may slaughter the innocent—better first to go and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day he reached Zhending. Muqali ordered him to assault the city, but Tianxiang asked, "An assault may kill innocents. Let me go first and explain the terms.

sentences.zh: 苟其不從，加兵未晚。」

translations.literal: If they do not comply, applying troops will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: If they refuse, we can still attack afterward."

sentences.zh: 木華黎許之。

translations.literal: Muqali agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali agreed.

sentences.zh: 天祥往見守將武仙，諭以禍福，仙悟，乃降。

translations.literal: Tianxiang went to see the defender Wu Xian, explained fortune and ruin, Xian understood, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang went to see the defender Wu Xian, explained the consequences of resistance and submission, and Xian surrendered.

sentences.zh: 吾也而請留天祥守真定，木華黎曰：「天下未定，智勇士可離左右乎？

translations.literal: Uyghur requested to leave Tianxiang to guard Zhending; Muqali said: "The realm is not yet settled—can wise brave men be kept from one's side?
translations.idiomatic: Uyghur asked to leave Tianxiang to guard Zhending. Muqali replied, "The realm is not yet settled. Can I keep a wise and brave man at my side?

sentences.zh: 吾將別處之。」

translations.literal: I shall place him elsewhere."
translations.idiomatic: I shall place him elsewhere."

sentences.zh: 乃以秉直之子天倪為河北西路兵馬都元帥，鎮真定；

translations.literal: Bingzhi's son Tianni was made Grand Marshal of Western Hebei army and horse, garrisoned at Zhending;
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhi's son Tianni was made Grand Marshal of the Western Hebei army and horse and stationed at Zhending;

sentences.zh: 以天祥為左副都元帥，餘如故，引兵南屯邢西遙水山下。

translations.literal: Tianxiang was made Left Vice Grand Marshal with the rest as before, and led troops south to encamp below Yaoshui Mountain west of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiang was made Left Vice Grand Marshal with his other duties unchanged, and led troops south to camp below Yaoshui Mountain west of Xing.

sentences.zh: 仙兄貴以萬人壁於山上，負固不下，天祥攜完顏胡速及黑軍百人，由鳥道扳援而上，盡掩捕之。

translations.literal: Xian's elder brother Gui with ten thousand men fortified on the mountain and held firm; Tianxiang took Wanyan Husu and a hundred Black Army men, climbed by bird paths hand over hand, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Xian's elder brother Gui fortified the mountain with ten thousand men and refused to yield. Tianxiang took Wanyan Husu and a hundred Black Army men up a narrow path hand over hand and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 仙驚曰：「公若有羽翼者，不然，何其能也！」

translations.literal: Xian in alarm said: "Sir, if you have wings—otherwise, how could you do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Xian exclaimed in alarm, "You must have wings, sir—how else could you have done this!"

sentences.zh: 遂下邢、磁、相三州。

translations.literal: He thereupon reduced Xing, Ci, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He then reduced the three prefectures of Xing, Ci, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 從戰黃龍岡，破單、勝、兗三州。

translations.literal: He followed in battle at Huanglong Ridge and broke Shan, Sheng, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Huanglong Ridge and captured the prefectures of Shan, Sheng, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 木華黎圍東平，久不下，怒吾也而不盡力，將手斬之，天祥請代攻。

translations.literal: Muqali besieged Dongping long without success, grew angry that Uyghur did not exert himself fully and would personally behead him; Tianxiang requested to attack in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali besieged Dongping for a long time without success. Enraged that Uyghur was not trying hard enough, he was about to behead him personally. Tianxiang asked to take over the assault.

sentences.zh: 木華黎喜，付皮甲一，又與己鐵鎧並被之。

translations.literal: Muqali was pleased, gave him one leather armor, and also put his own iron armor on him together.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali was delighted, gave him a leather coat of armor, and placed his own iron armor on him as well.

sentences.zh: 鏖戰不已，木華黎使人止之曰：「爾力竭矣，宜少休。」

translations.literal: The fierce battle continued without cease; Muqali sent someone to stop him: "Your strength is spent—you should rest a little."
translations.idiomatic: The fierce fighting continued without pause. Muqali sent word to stop him: "Your strength is spent. Rest awhile."

sentences.zh: 復以金鞍名馬與之。

translations.literal: He again gave him a gold saddle and famous horse.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave him a gold saddle and a fine horse.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，從取綏德、鄜、坊等五十餘城。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he followed in taking Guide, Fu, Fang, and more than fifty cities.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day he helped capture Guide, Fu, Fang, and more than fifty other cities.

sentences.zh: 壬午，木華黎攻青龍、金勝諸堡，花帽軍堅守不下，既破，欲屠之，天祥力諫而止，獲壯士五千人。

translations.literal: On the day renwu Muqali attacked Qinglong, Jinsheng and other forts; the Flower-Cap Army held firm; once broken he wished to slaughter them; Tianxiang strongly remonstrated and stopped it, obtaining five thousand stalwart warriors.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day Muqali attacked the forts of Qinglong and Jinsheng. The Flower-Cap Army held firm. After they fell, Muqali wished to slaughter the defenders. Tianxiang protested strongly and stopped him, securing five thousand stalwart warriors instead.

sentences.zh: 癸未春，還軍河中，木華黎上其功，賜金虎符，授蒙古漢軍兵馬都元帥，總十二萬戶，鎮河中。

translations.literal: In the spring of the year guiwei he returned his army to Hezhong; Muqali reported his merit; he was granted a golden tiger tally, made Marshal of Mongol and Han Armies, commanded twelve ten-thousand-households, and garrisoned Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of guiwei year he withdrew his army to Hezhong. Muqali reported his achievements, and he received a golden tiger tally and was appointed Marshal of Mongol and Han Armies, commanding twelve ten-thousand-households and garrisoning Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 冬，徇西夏，破賀蘭山。

translations.literal: In winter he campaigned against Western Xia and broke Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he campaigned against Western Xia and captured Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 還，遇賊，射傷額，出血，目為之昏。

translations.literal: On the return he encountered bandits; an arrow wounded his forehead, blood flowed, and his eyes were dimmed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he encountered bandits. An arrow struck his forehead, blood flowed, and his vision was clouded.

sentences.zh: 甲申，歸北京，授右副北京等七路兵馬都元帥。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen he returned to Beijing and was made Right Vice Marshal of the Seven Circuits of Beijing and others.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day he returned to Beijing and was appointed Right Vice Marshal of the Seven Circuits of Beijing and other regions.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朝太宗於盧朐河，乞致仕，不允。

translations.literal: On the day gengyin he had audience with Taizong at the Luju River, begged to retire, and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin day he had audience with Ögedei Khan at the Luju River and asked to retire, but his request was denied.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，太宗用兵河南，強之從行，轉漕河上，給餉諸軍。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao Taizong used troops in Henan, compelled him to follow the campaign, transported grain along the river, and supplied provisions to the armies.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day Ögedei Khan campaigned in Henan and compelled him to accompany the expedition. He transported grain along the river and supplied provisions to the armies.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，命天祥領汴京百工數千，屯霸州之益津，行元帥府事，賜錦衣一襲。

translations.literal: On the day renchen Tianxiang was ordered to lead several thousand artisans of Bianjing, encamped at Yijin in Bazhou, acted as marshal headquarters, and was granted one suit of brocade robes.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Tianxiang was ordered to lead several thousand artisans from Bianjing, encamped at Yijin in Bazhou, and acted as marshal headquarters. He was granted a suit of brocade robes.

sentences.zh: 初，天祥夜中流矢，鏃入頰骨，不能出，至是，金瘡再發，鏃自口出。

translations.literal: Earlier Tianxiang had been struck by an arrow at night; the arrowhead entered his cheekbone and could not be removed; now the wound broke open again and the arrowhead came out through his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Tianxiang had been struck by an arrow at night; the arrowhead lodged in his cheekbone and could not be removed. Now the wound reopened, and the arrowhead came out through his mouth.

sentences.zh: 睿宗聞而閔之，授海濱和眾利州等處總管，兼領霸州御衣局人匠都達魯花赤，行北京七路兵馬都元帥府事。

translations.literal: Prince Ruizong heard and pitied him, appointing him Chief Administrator of Haibin, Hezhong, Lizhou and other places, concurrently commanding the darughachi of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau artisans at Bazhou, and acting as marshal headquarters of the Seven Circuits of Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Tolui heard and took pity on him. He was appointed Chief Administrator of Haibin, Hezhong, Lizhou, and other districts, concurrently made darughachi of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau artisans at Bazhou, and placed in charge of the marshal headquarters of the Seven Circuits of Beijing.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，俾仍舊職。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne, he was ordered to retain his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke Khan took the throne, he was ordered to retain his former post.

sentences.zh: 戊午秋九月，以疾卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn of the year wuwu he died of illness at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of autumn in wuwu year he died of illness at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 天祥幼有大志，長身駢脅，力絕人，性不嗜酒，喜稼穡，好施予。

translations.literal: Tianxiang from youth had great ambition, a tall frame with broad ribs, strength surpassing others, a nature not fond of wine, delighting in farming, and loving to give.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Tianxiang harbored great ambition. He was tall and powerfully built, with strength beyond ordinary men. He did not drink, loved farming, and was generous in giving.

sentences.zh: 乙未括戶，縱其奴千餘口，俾為民。

translations.literal: On the day yiwei when households were registered, he released more than a thousand of his slaves and made them civilians.
translations.idiomatic: During the yiwei household registration he freed more than a thousand of his slaves and made them civilians.

sentences.zh: 晚雖喪明，憂國愛民之心，未嘗忘也。

translations.literal: In his later years though he lost his sight, his heart of concern for the state and love for the people was never forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Though he lost his sight in later years, he never forgot his concern for the state and love for the people.

sentences.zh: 子彬，江東提刑按察副使；

translations.literal: His son Bin was Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangdong;
translations.idiomatic: His son Bin was Vice Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangdong;

sentences.zh: 槐，襲霸州御衣局人匠都達魯花赤。

translations.literal: Huai succeeded as Darughachi of the Bazhou Imperial Wardrobe Bureau Artisans.
translations.idiomatic: and Huai succeeded as Darughachi of the Bazhou Imperial Wardrobe Bureau Artisans.
